checks.name: One monotonic whole-readiness budget and bounded individual attempts
checks.result: Production starts a Stopwatch for readiness and converts validated WaitSeconds to a bounded 1000..120000 ms budget. Each attempt is bounded by min(overall budget, elapsed+2000), and every wait receives floor(max(0, deadline-elapsed)) milliseconds. The retry sleep is bounded by min(300, overall remaining). There are no Get-Date or Invoke-WebRequest calls. Both post-dispatch and post-completion/cleanup checks reject elapsed>=whole budget. Status 200 additionally requires elapsed<attempt deadline, preventing late per-attempt success from being published.

checks.name: Fractional and final-boundary acceptance
checks.evidenceType: source and actual-harness inspection; PowerShell scenarios not executed locally
checks.result: The source uses TotalMilliseconds rather than truncated elapsed milliseconds. A completed result at 999.5/1000 ms can remain timely; exact 1000 or 1000.5 is rejected. An already-completed result is read without a wait even when floor(remaining)=0; unfinished sub-millisecond remainder is rejected conservatively. Inspected 18 harness cases exercising the actual AST-extracted production loop, including late/exact/after/full/attempt boundaries, dispatch and cleanup advancement, both wall-clock jumps, child exit, retry sleep and retry wait budgets. The harness verifies one Boolean output, not incidental method output.

checks.name: Final owned-child acceptance and initialization order
checks.evidenceType: source reasoning and executed static assertions
checks.result: HTTP type/assembly initialization completes before Process.Start, so a compilation/load failure cannot strand a newly owned child. The loop refreshes the same Process object and checks HasExited; the outer caller rechecks the deadline and fresh child state before printing success. Failure kills only that retained Process object when still alive, without PID/name lookup. The actual outer IfStatementAst is exercised by four synthetic final-acceptance cases in the Windows harness, including an unrelated fake process that must remain untouched. BOM/CRLF and initialization order static checks passed locally.

checks.name: Managed HTTP lifetime and bounded memory use
checks.evidenceType: source reasoning and primary documentation corroboration
checks.result: ReadStatusAsync uses ResponseHeadersRead and returns only an integer status; it never buffers or parses a response body. The response, request, HttpClient and owned handler have nested using lifetimes, including late responses. ConfigureAwait(false) and managed cancellation avoid PowerShell scriptblocks on foreign thread-pool runspaces. Production handler disables redirects, proxy use and default credentials. The readiness loop has finite retry delays within a maximum 120-second total budget; it cannot create an unbounded sequence of probes. Uncooperative underlying operations can outlive a timed-out individual attempt, but they retain cleanup ownership and do not extend the main wait.

checks.name: Cancellation/finish interleavings
checks.result: Cancel marks cancellationRequested and cancellationQueued while holding gate, then queues actual CTS.Cancel away from the waiting PowerShell thread. Duplicate calls are no-ops. If work finishes first, it marks finished and disposes the source without queuing cancellation. If cancellation is queued/running, finish defers disposal; the worker clears cancellationQueued and disposes only after finished. This prevents disposal during CTS cancellation and keeps a blocked callback off the readiness path. A late response remains owned by the asynchronous using/finally chain. I found no concrete double-disposal, early-disposal or lost-response path within the production ownership contract.

It does not replace the production C# transport algorithm. Six cases cover timely 200, 503, synchronous send failure, cancellation-ignoring late response, honored cancellation and a blocked cancellation callback. Assertions require one send, zero body reads, cleanup of request/response/handler/source, no timed-out cancellation gate and retained source ownership while work is pending. All handler work is in memory; no real child, socket, credential or policy operation is needed.

findings.title: Compound numeric prefixes evade radix classification and expose positive suffix evidence
findings.impact: Unsupported numeric-looking counts/durations become high-confidence blocks and one offline deny candidate in brute-force, web-injection, persistence, privilege and exfiltration. Independent brute-force matching repeats the same erroneous extraction.
findings.rootCause: NUMERIC_FRAGMENT recognizes punctuation, underscores, whitespace and format characters inside a whole numeric-looking span. RADIX_FRAGMENT_START only recognizes an optional sign followed by one contiguous N+ run, optional space/underscore and then x/b/o. For 0.0xFF, 1.0xFF, 0_0xFF or 0+format+0xFF, that narrow anchored prefix test fails. Completed-unit recognition then treats the later xFF/F/U/UL tail as a unit and inserts a boundary before the final evidence integer. The later radix guard uses the same predicate, so it also fails to suppress the suffix.

findings.recommendedFix: Use a consistent whole-fragment grammar for both segment formation and radix rejection. An interior radix/type-looking tail must not become a unit merely because an earlier numeric component prevents a simple anchored zero-prefix match. Preserve a complete unsupported compound token, retaining explicit clause boundaries and genuine metadata units. Cover hexadecimal, binary and octal compound variants plus nonzero/Unicode/separator controls without importing helpers into standalone judge files.
findings.scope: No request to accept or numerically evaluate these unsupported tokens; the defect is manufacturing positive evidence from their suffixes.

findings.title: A real zero-valued baud unit is classified as a binary fragment and suppresses independent evidence
findings.impact: Unrelated Metric 0baud metadata suppresses otherwise valid count/time evidence across all five deciders. The same description with 1baud, 0bytes or 0objects correctly preserves the block and candidate, so an unrelated metric value changes the outcome.
findings.rootCause: radixFragment treats a zero followed by b/o as radix syntax when the remaining letters all belong to [A-Fa-fpPnNuUlL]. The normal unit baud has b followed by aud; every remaining letter happens to fall in that set. Thus the real word unit is rejected as a numeric fragment despite the stated policy to preserve ordinary word units. The predicate loses the distinction between a unit and an arbitrary mixture of hexadecimal/type-suffix letters.

findings.rootCause: The completed metadata candidate contains unit B/s, but the independent fragment locator ends at 0B. The classifier rejects that truncated stem as radix, preventing the compact comma boundary. A following space allows the separate evidence matcher to rediscover 20, masking the inconsistent unit extent.
findings.repairRequirement: Classify the complete candidate quantity and complete unit extent together. Boundary creation and evidence rejection must share the same span decision rather than comparing a full B/s unit with a truncated 0B fragment.

recommendedArchitecture.approach: Keep the bounded standalone reader contract, but use one component-aware quantity classifier for both creation of numeric boundaries and protection against suffix extraction.
steps: Locate a proposed quantity using original string offsets. Classify its complete numeric prefix and entire unit together, including slash compounds such as B/s; a shorter overlapping numeric fragment is not the complete candidate.

Scan the retained numeric prefix component by component across the already supported numeric connectors. Preserve a recognized unsupported radix component through ordinary comma/period/space/format connections. An anchored check at the first character is insufficient.

Recognize numeric-looking radix syntax structurally. For b/o, a numeric body or the existing incomplete-marker form is different from a complete alphabetic unit word such as baud. Recognition is deliberately broader than valid arithmetic: a numeric body with a digit invalid for that base must still remain unsupported, rather than becoming an ordinary unit.

Emit a soft boundary only after a separately completed, genuine metadata quantity. Preserve hard clause terminators as independent reset points. Later evidence must not retroactively alter an earlier completed metadata boundary.

Reuse that classification in integerEvidence so candidate extraction cannot reopen a span already deemed unsupported. After a boundary is established, retain the existing whole ASCII integer, safe-integer, digit-length and detector-threshold rules.
contractsToPreserve: Do not turn Unicode metadata digits into accepted ASCII evidence. Retain the existing Unicode zero recognition for syntax classification, and keep metadata recognition distinct from evidence validation.
Preserve all existing Unicode 15/17 zero and formatted/scientific metadata positive controls; this design does not require metadata numbers to satisfy the evidence-integer grammar.

Keep the original 1,024 UTF-16-code-unit description bound and original UTF-16 source offsets. A code-point scanner must advance offsets by code-point width rather than substitute code-point indices or normalized text.

Retain compact supported evidence, count/time thresholds, hard-clause independence, structured-field precedence, standalone decide exports and no-import modules. Copy one identical local helper into the six existing readers rather than adding a judge-side module dependency.
recommendedArchitecture.boundedness: A bounded forward classification over the existing description is sufficient; another list of compound prefixes, unit exceptions or Unicode spellings is not required.
recommendedArchitecture.ambiguityLimit: Scientific F or similarly ambiguous literal/unit spellings are not blockers and are not used in this matrix. No arbitrary natural-language or new unit-recognition policy is proposed.

report.conclusion: The broader failure is supported by the existing grammar, without declaring unknown unit words invalid. A completed-unit candidate cannot establish independence by restarting inside an earlier opaque alphanumeric quantity. The current code recovers a full quantity start but never proves that the complete prefix before its proposed unit is a numeric metadata spelling.
contractReasoning: The current completed regex accepts an alphabetic unit word (optionally slash-separated) and then a delimiter before another numeric expression. Its grammar does not accept a digit embedded inside that same unit word or two adjacent quantities without a delimiter.
Accordingly, 1abc and 1quux may be legitimate completed metadata under this broad grammar. This review does not claim those words are unknown and therefore forbidden.

In 1abc1F, choosing the suffix 1F leaves the earlier 1abc unconsumed. There is neither a separator between abc and the following 1 nor a whole supported unit abc1F. The interior suffix cannot justify a new boundary after the final period.

In contrast, 1e3F has a complete scientific numeric prefix 1e3 and a unit F. It remains eligible as completed metadata. Whether F also has a programming-language suffix meaning is not used as a reason to reject it.

The R4 radix predicate only rejects a zero-prefixed b/o body when its first stripped character is numeric. It therefore misses 0bA1F, but expanding only that predicate does not address 1abc1F or 1baud1F. The shared eligibility gap is the whole numeric prefix.

repairDesign.proposedGate: Before adding a completed-unit boundary, validate the entire source slice from the retained quantity start to the proposed unit start as a metadata-number spelling. A local digit+unit match is only a candidate, never proof by itself.
details: Fully consume the prefix. Allow the existing numeric Unicode characters and supported formatting/grouping characters, plus complete scientific exponent syntax needed by 1e3, 1E+3 and −1.25e-3. Do not accept an arbitrary alphabetic word before an interior digit.
Keep this a lexical recognition step, not a Number()/safe-integer/value check. Metadata may be grouped, non-ASCII or scientific and does not itself become detector evidence.

Keep the complete unit extent (including B/s) and delimiter separate. Do not accept an interior F/ms candidate if preceding numeric-prefix text is unrecognized. Unknown complete alphabetic unit words should remain allowed under the existing grammar.

Use the same whole-span eligibility result when creating boundaries and preventing later suffix re-entry. Existing radix/whole-token guards must not be bypassed simply because one candidate's prefix was rejected.
Retain hard clause resets and already completed prior quantities, so 1abc 1F.20 and 1quux1F;20 continue to expose independent later evidence.
Retain original UTF-16 positions and the 1,024-code-unit input limit. Do not normalize Unicode metadata into ASCII or replace original positions with code-point indices.

Leave safe ASCII integer evidence, digit limits, thresholds, structured-field precedence and standalone exports/import constraints unchanged. Use identical local helper semantics across all six existing readers.
repairDesign.whyNotAnotherRadixRule: A body-scanning fix limited to zero-prefixed b/o fragments still accepts opaque prefixes such as 1abc1. Full-prefix eligibility addresses the common missing proof and preserves scientific metadata through a positive numeric-spelling grammar.
repairDesign.ambiguityLimit: No known-unit dictionary, arbitrary-unit exception list or new rejection of scientific F is proposed. These findings concern interior matching against the existing grammar, not the real-world meaning of an unknown unit.

findings.title: A non-ASCII alphabetic prefix without an earlier digit is still bypassed when starting integer evidence
findings.origin: Fresh independent reviewer source inspection and canonical-equivalence challenge. Not a peer/current-round finding or parent-supplied counterexample.
findings.rootCause: Both INTEGER_TOKEN and NUMERIC_FRAGMENT retain an ASCII A-Za-z-only left boundary, while a numeric ownership span must begin with a number. When Á20 or NaＮ20 contains no earlier numeric component, the fragment finder starts directly at20. The ownership guard sees no earlier owner, and the post-match previous-character guard rejects marks/modifier letters but not ordinary non-ASCII Lu/Ll letters. Therefore the suffix is admitted as a new evidence integer. The Unicode continuation repair works once a number already owns the span but leaves this entry path unchanged.

findings.title: Completed-quantity candidates repeatedly rescan every suffix of an allowed long numeric run
findings.location: xdr/brute-force/decide.mjs:83 and 86 (candidate regex starts), 131-134 (both scans); same numeric helper block in xdr/brute-force/match.mjs, xdr/web-injection/decide.mjs, xdr/persistence/decide.mjs, xdr/privilege/decide.mjs and xdr/exfiltration/decide.mjs
findings.rootCause: Unanchored numeric-run candidates retry at each interior digit when the required quantity terminator is absent. Greedy N+ then backtracks over the remaining run at each candidate start. R6 combines two such scans on every numericFragments invocation; the brute-force public path invokes that helper twelve times. This amplifies pre-existing quadratic work rather than introducing an unbounded input length.
findings.impact: The allowed 1024-character error/unsupported-quantity path uses approximately half a second of synchronous CPU per brute-force decision on the measured environment. Five alerts consume about 2.8 seconds in public decision calculation, and the actual candidate builder separately spends 2.67 seconds returning no candidates for five already-alert records. This is a concrete avoidable batch-processing regression within current limits, not a failure inferred solely from one timing or an invented performance SLA.
findings.reproducer: Use a valid synthetic brute-force alert with timestamp 2026-11-23T10:00:00.000Z, srcip 192.0.2.1, srcuser resource_fixture, level 12, no structured count, and description (Korean same-source login-failure prefix + repeated ASCII 9).slice(0,1024). Call the actual decide function after one warmup; compare lengths 128/256/512/1024. For integration, call actual buildDenyCandidates with five such valid-id alerts and corresponding action=alert decisions; it returns [] after the measured synchronous work. The saved probe imposes independent five-second child deadlines.
findings.causalEvidence: R6 1024-character median 568.687 ms; R5 138.124 ms; direct actual import 535.101–555.848 ms; paired candidate scans 45.130 ms per numericFragments invocation; twelve such invocations. Preventing only interior numeric-run candidate restarts in an in-memory diagnostic control yields the identical alert result in median 2.270 ms.
findings.repair: Locate completed-quantity candidates only at maximal numeric-component starts, or use a deterministic span scanner that advances once over a numeric run before considering its unit. Preserve the Unicode/Korean ownership semantics and malformed-token rejection. Keep all six mirrored helpers consistent. Reuse parsed numeric spans within a decision where practical rather than redoing identical work per quantity query. The diagnostic lookbehind is evidence of the cause, not permission to skip the independent lexical regression suite.
findings.validationNeeded: Retain the semantic cap and Unicode/numeric lexical tests; add a focused long-no-unit run negative control with scaling or deterministic scan-work evidence and a small-batch integration check. Confirm positive short quantities and independent following quantities retain their established outcomes. Avoid a brittle absolute millisecond SLA as the only regression assertion.

root_cause.reference_source_observation: Framework HttpClient links the caller token to its pending-request source. report.rootCause: Native dispatchEvent does not await the returned async create-form handler. Test finally released a deferred session refresh but teardown immediately restored/deleted global document before the handler final DOM update. Subsequent fixtures could conceal the leak.
report.repair: Observe actual create-form submit handler promises while retaining native EventTarget dispatch/return/error and listener identity semantics. Boundedly drain all settlements with a real captured5second timer before restoring globals in finally. Add a subprocess regression that executes the original focus case alone, excludes inherited NODE_TEST_CONTEXT from a copied environment, and checks that exactly one test passed.
report.scope: Only test/session-invalidation-ui.test.mjs changes. No product/runtime/config/current-documentation changes. Detached void loadNotes work is explicitly outside this tracker scope.
report.preflightRefinement: Root changed the initial fail-fast Promise.all drain to Promise.allSettled so one handler rejection cannot restore globals while another handler remains pending. The owner preserved the initial source/logs separately; no published product behavior was affected.

report.root_cause: The fixture restored global DOM state before its create-form submit handler finished processing the deferred refresh. Existing tests asserted the intermediate focus state, then resolved refresh in finally without owning the actual event handler completion. The handler later reached syncCreatePendingState against removed globals. Neighboring test fixtures could mask this lifetime error.
changes: Track only actual Promise results from create-form submit listeners in this fixture. Native dispatchEvent is unchanged; wrappers return the original callback value and preserve function this and object.handleEvent invocation. Stable callback wrappers let native EventTarget retain capture/once/duplicate-registration/removal behavior.

Wait in t.after for all currently started submit completions using allSettled, repeating if a handler started another owned submission. A single 5-second timer imported from node:timers remains real despite mocked globals. An unresolved handler fails cleanup rather than waiting without limit.

Record callback rejection and throw AggregateError after all owned submissions settle, while continuing to return the original Promise to EventTarget so its existing rejection behavior is retained. Restore globals in finally even if cleanup fails.

Add one child-process regression selecting the original failing focus test alone. Copy the environment and exclude NODE_TEST_CONTEXT case-insensitively; preserve the parent environment. The exact name filter excludes the new parent regression, preventing recursion, and assertions require one actual pass with zero skips.

All eight existing delayed-refresh family tests and their UI assertions remain unchanged. No product document guard, arbitrary tick delay, sleep, button-state completion heuristic or broad EventTarget replacement.

preflight_correction.issue: Parent and reviewer2 independently identified that Promise.all could restore globals after one rejection while another handler was pending. The draft had passed its current focused/file tests but did not satisfy this failure-ordering contract.
preflight_correction.resolution: Replaced the drain snapshot wait with Promise.allSettled; errors are propagated only after owned completions settle or the real deadline expires. All listed final-source tests were executed again with fresh logs.

findings.title: Four browser readers can publish successful results after the deadline or cancellation during their final await
findings.root_cause: Inner body readers check their monotonic deadline after parsing, then fulfill their work promise. The outer await Promise.race(...) adds a separate microtask continuation. None of these four wrappers rechecks lifetime at that final publication boundary. A microtask already queued between the inner check and outer continuation can abort the request or occupy the event loop beyond the deadline; timer callbacks cannot run until those microtasks drain. The already-settled work result therefore wins and is returned/rendered. Generation checks in operations and device callers do not establish that the request deadline still holds.
findings.reproduction: The final reader.read() fixture queues two nested microtasks and returns Promise.resolve({done:true}). The inner read continuation finishes and passes its last check; the queued callback then either occupies 35 ms of monotonic time or aborts the caller, before the outer race continuation resumes. Use a 10 ms request budget. No real network, authentication, packaging or deployment is used. See the two exact-source proof artifacts in tests.
findings.observed_impact: The local app helper reports a successful response even after caller cancellation or expiry. The device helper and inline remote helper also return expired success, allowing later caller processing; the operations UI demonstrably renders a snapshot after its request budget. These are correctness/lifecycle contract violations, not evidence of authorization bypass.
findings.repair: Capture the result of the final awaited race and check the monotonic deadline, abort state and relevant epoch immediately before returning or applying it. In operations, check again after synchronous snapshot validation and before render. Ensure error-result publication has an intentional policy too: retain independently confirmed HTTP denial/status distinctions and do not turn them into successful data; do not accidentally bypass or remove readHttpJson's auth-lock header-transport draining for cookie-changing requests. Keep bounded cleanup nonblocking. Add deterministic microtask-interleaving regressions for success, caller cancellation, timeout, local error and timely observed HTTP denial at the final publication boundary across all four siblings.

findings.title: Brute-force raw evidence projections disagree in description and textual-count boundaries
findings.rootCause: The isolated decider inspects and extracts textual failure counts from up to 1,024 raw description characters. The matcher uses the sanitized 512-character display projection for pattern semantics but parses textual counts from the unbounded original description. These three different projections make corroboration disagree with the local judge in both directions.
findings.evidence: A supported raw bf-02 with 550 leading spaces (584 total description characters) retains block/.97/cross_account_password_spray in decide but yields matcher null and zero candidates. Conversely, use a supported raw alert with description "Failed login from the same IP within 5 minutes. " + 1100 spaces + "50 failed login attempts" and no numeric data count. decide returns alert/.65; matcher extracts 50 beyond the judge limit and returns rapid_source_login_failures/.96. A forged block/.96 proposal is then accepted as one candidate, despite contradicting the local judge.
findings.impact: Both omission of a valid strong response candidate and acceptance of a proposal inconsistent with the judge are reproducible in local synthetic inputs. The mismatch concerns raw alert evidence, not a requirement that five-field display projections preserve intentionally removed information.
findings.recommendedFix: Use one consistent bounded raw description projection for classification and textual count extraction in decide and independent matcher, preserving the sanitized/redacted output projection separately. Retain standalone judge isolation. Add both long-description directions, explicit numeric counts, and no-count/beyond-boundary cases. Define field precedence or reject ambiguous hybrid raw/normalized inputs consistently instead of broadening acceptance.
findings.similarPaths: Only brute-force has a separate matcher. Its raw and normalized branches, scalar failure-count fields and textual failure-count parsing should follow consistent evidence bounds; the five sibling builders recompute their local decider.
scopeEvidence: xdr/README.md documents raw Wazuh-shaped fixtures and three-field judge responses.

Conflicting raw and normalized aliases produce different metadata precedence in decide and matcher, but their ambiguous input contract is not established. This is not a standalone finding and no permissive acceptance is requested.

findings.title: Brute-force candidate builder accepts confidence outside the decision contract
findings.rootCause: A lower-bound comparison alone coerces strings and does not reject undefined, NaN or values above one; the supplied confidence is copied into the candidate instead of requiring a valid, matching corroborated confidence.
findings.evidence: For unchanged strong bf-02 input, replace the valid decision's confidence with undefined, string 0.97, numeric 2 or NaN. Every case creates one candidate; checkZTNAExtra returns deny with an otherwise valid synthetic context.
findings.impact: Malformed decision data violates the documented numeric 0..1 decision contract yet becomes a usable simulated deny candidate. This is not evidence of a live deployment bypass.
findings.recommendedFix: Require finite numeric confidence in [0.85,1] and agreement with independently derived evidence confidence, then retain the verified value. Add invalid/missing/string and wrong-but-finite confidence cases.
findings.similarPaths: The five sibling candidate builders already compare proposal confidence with independently recomputed decision confidence. Keep consistent rejection semantics.

findings.title: Truthy non-boolean values satisfy brute-force server-attestation gate
findings.rootCause: The brute-force helper tests truthiness of verifiedByServer while all five sibling gates require exact boolean true.
findings.evidence: Build one valid bf-02 candidate and supply matching synthetic address/account/time. verifiedByServer=false yields pass, but verifiedByServer='false', 1 or {} yields deny, exactly like true.
findings.impact: Malformed context can be treated as explicitly server-attested by the exported simulation helper. There is no claimed browser-to-live-gate exploit or established production integration.
findings.recommendedFix: Require trustedContext.verifiedByServer === true before evaluating any scoped rule, and add false/missing/string/number/object boundary cases while retaining upstream deny/step_up preservation.
findings.similarPaths: Other five checkZTNAExtra implementations already use exact true; apply the same boolean provenance contract here.

findings.title: Connection manager accepts or publishes work after the lookup/start deadline across its final await
findings.root_cause: within() checks its deadline before resolving and then clears its timer. The generic start continuation checks only sentinels, aborted signal and closed state before registering a flow; it does not check its existing absolute deadline. Generic and active native locate continuations similarly accept a formerly timely within() result after expiry, and the outer finish/status/cancel methods do not retain a lookup deadline through their own final await. Timer task callbacks cannot enforce the bound while queued microtasks run between these continuations.
findings.impact: An expired start can register a new flow and return 201. An expired pre-acceptance identity lookup can still launch a separate redeem job and return 202, or mutate a flow to cancelled and return 200, contrary to the documented 504/no-state-change deadline contract. The evidence establishes lifecycle correctness defects, not an authorization bypass.
findings.reproduction: Run the manager-boundary, manager-acceptance and native-acceptance scratch probes listed in tests. They use synthetic scope/HTTP responses, deterministic monotonic clocks and queued microtask permutations; timers are deliberately not fired, representing the same scheduling boundary in which the timer task has not yet run. The start probe observes the actual flow registration timestamp to distinguish late mutation from merely late caller observation.
findings.repair: Carry an absolute operation/lookup deadline to the synchronous state-publication or acceptance boundary. Check it after every awaited helper and again immediately before flows.set, changing state, or dispatching the independent job. Do not rely solely on changing within(), since callers add further await continuations. Apply the same policy to all generic/native locate consumers and the generic context resolver using within(). Preserve late-capability disposal, bounded cancellation cleanup, the no-state-change 504 contract, and the independence of work already validly accepted as 202. Add final-await scheduling tests for both positive and negative results and all affected methods.

findings.title: Generic background completion can settle connected after its independent finish deadline
findings.root_cause: The manager represents its background-job finishTimeoutMs only with a timer. After connector.complete() finishes, its final scope verification starts a fresh scopeTimeoutMs budget, checks only flow identity/state, and may settle connected after the original job deadline while the timer task is delayed. Successful settlement then clears that timer. The connector's own operation deadline does not cover the manager's additional final verification.
findings.impact: The manager reports connected even though its own declared background completion budget expired; the expected terminal timeout/unknown state is skipped. A credential may already have been persisted, so timeout handling must preserve outcome uncertainty and must not imply automatic grant revocation.
findings.reproduction: Run a2-r1-reviewer2-manager-background.mjs. Actual exported manager plus real connector, synthetic response/vault fixtures, finishTimeoutMs=10 and scopeTimeoutMs=100: the tenth scope callback (manager's post-connector verification) advances monotonic time to 11. Observed stored=1, finalStatus=200, finalState=connected. No live credential or network is involved.
findings.repair: Record a monotonic deadline on the accepted job, bound final verification by the smaller of the remaining job budget and scope budget, and recheck that absolute deadline immediately before terminal state publication. Use the existing timeout/unknown outcome when expired. Keep this job deadline independent of the already-completed initiating HTTP request and retain closure/cancellation ownership guards. Audit the native final-settlement path against its capability's independent absolute deadline rather than changing accepted-job behavior blindly.

findings.title: Pre-dispatch auth expiry inside the HTTP lifetime is incorrectly reported as an uncertain server outcome
findings.root_cause: After readHttpJson has installed its abort listener, the final checkRequest before fetch can expire and abort the controller while dispatched remains false. onStopped immediately rejects requestExpired as AUTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT without inspecting dispatched. findings.title: Response adapters use literal spelling instead of IP identity for gates, grouping and benign precedence
findings.rootCause: The parser accepts multiple valid IPv6 spellings, but response adapters retain them as raw string keys and compare them with strict string equality. The same discrepancy is copied into normalSources/benignDestinations exclusion sets and candidate grouping hashes.
findings.impact: Equivalent addresses can miss a scoped simulated denial, produce duplicate scopes, or bypass the adapters' documented conservative normal-source/benign-destination protection. This is demonstrated only in offline synthetic adapter behavior; no live engine or enforcement bypass is claimed.
reproduction: In each of the six modules, clone the first strong raw fixture, set source to 2001:db8::1234, and supply all required true attestation/binding flags with matching account/path/event/time. Known-CVE receives a synthetic /notes URL for its existing route requirement. The resulting one candidate denies the identical source spelling. Changing only the trusted source to 2001:0DB8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:1234 returns pass in every module, although both parse as IPv6 and the independent oracle returns the same identity.

All six modules also miss equivalence for fe80::1234%eth0 versus FE80:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:1234%eth0, and for ::ffff:192.0.2.1 versus ::ffff:c000:201. Both latter forms remain IPv6; no IPv4-family equivalence is asserted.

Two otherwise identical strong alerts with unique event IDs group into one candidate when the address spelling is identical, but two candidates when only the equivalent source spelling differs, across all six modules.

For web-injection, known-cve, persistence and privilege, add a genuine record fixture with the same source: the builder correctly suppresses candidates. Change only that normal source to an equivalent IPv6 spelling and one candidate incorrectly reappears.

Exfiltration shows the same missed gate and split grouping for destination 2001:db8::abcd versus 2001:0DB8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:ABCD. Its benign-destination fixture suppresses the candidate at the identical spelling but fails to do so at the equivalent spelling.
identityRequirements: Validate an address literal before normalization; do not turn invalid strings or hostnames into addresses.
Within one address family, compare actual address value rather than hexadecimal case, omitted zero groups or dotted versus hexadecimal IPv6 suffix spelling.
Preserve the exact IPv6 zone/interface identifier: eth0 and eth1 are distinct scopes. Zone identifiers are not assumed case-insensitive.
Preserve address family. Native IPv4 192.0.2.1 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 ::ffff:192.0.2.1 remain distinct without an explicit cross-family contract.
Preserve existing account, path, agent, event, device/session binding and upstream-decision requirements. Normalization cannot supply missing provenance.
findings.recommendedFix: Use one validated address-identity operation consistently in offline adapter gate comparisons, source/destination grouping and benign-evidence exclusion sets. Keep isolated judge entries import-free and keep original fixtures unchanged. Add positive equivalent-spelling and negative distinct-address/family/zone regressions at the full builder-to-gate boundary.

findings.title: Brute-force gate accepts matching non-IP strings as an address binding
findings.rootCause: The shared stored-candidate validator requires only a nonempty source string. Five adapters additionally check trusted source with isIP, but brute-force only checks nonemptiness; matching two malformed strings therefore satisfies its source binding.
findings.impact: Malformed stored/context data can produce a simulated deny despite lacking a valid IP address. The normal builder rejects such addresses, but the exported gate's stored-input validation remains incomplete compared with its sibling adapters.
findings.reproduction: Build a valid strong brute-force candidate, then set both rule.sourceAddress and trustedContext.sourceAddress to localhost, not-an-ip, 192.000.2.1 or 2001:db8::gggg. Keep valid evidence, time, account, confidence and verifiedByServer=true. node:net.isIP returns 0 for every value, yet checkZTNAExtra returns deny for all four.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a successfully validated address identity for the brute-force trusted source and consumed candidate source. This can share the operation used for the first finding. Malformed values must return pass without binding; retain upstream deny/step_up preservation.

tests.result: PASS
Confirmed three manifestations of one wall-clock defect
tests.detail: Executed actual generic manager with synthetic scope/HTTP only and a naturally advancing clock Date.now()+offset. A 1-second rollback evicts the newer completed record. At 60 ms actual monotonic elapsed, retainMs=30 expires without offset (404) but survives with rollback (200). At less than 1 ms elapsed, retainMs=600000 retains without offset (200) but expires with +600001 ms wall adjustment (404).

findings.rootCause: Adjustable wall-clock settledAt is used both to order completed operations and measure relative retention. This confuses observation timestamps with elapsed duration/completion order.
findings.impact: After a normal clock adjustment, the newly promised oldest-completion eviction can discard the newest usable result instead. Recent results can also disappear immediately after a forward adjustment or outlive retainMs after rollback. The map remains capacity-bounded, so this is a retention/recovery correctness issue rather than unbounded growth.
reproduction: Create actual generic manager with maxFlows=2, synthetic verified scope and /start response; start/cancel A at wall T; move injected wall to T-1000; start/cancel B; start C. status(A)=200, status(B)=404, status(C)=200. Actual completion order says A should be reclaimed first.
With retainMs=30 and clock=Date.now()+offset, cancel a flow and wait 60 ms measured by performance.now(): control offset=0 yields 404; offset=-1000 yields 200.
With retainMs=600000 and the same advancing clock, cancel a flow and read within less than 1 ms monotonic elapsed: control offset=0 yields 200; offset=+600001 yields 404.
findings.recommendation: Use monotonic elapsed time for retainMs and monotonic completion order/time for capacity eviction. Keep wall-clock timestamps for external absolute expiry/provenance. Apply consistently to generic/native settlement, pruning, final acceptance and native connected-to-unknown transition; preserve existing post-await lifetime checks. Test clock adjustments in both directions plus terminal records completed in an order different from their start order.

findings.title: Device UI publishes registration/authentication facts and advances ceremonies before validating successful response semantics
contracts: api/device.js:111-113: aleph.device.status.v1, known registration enum, verified/canOpenVault boolean relationship, installIsApproval=false
src/device-access.mjs:3,16-18: current proof consumer grammar /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,100}$/u; generator's 43-character output does not narrow that contract
findings.rootCause: Transport success and parseable JSON are treated as sufficient evidence of a domain state. Status falls through all missing/unknown fields to 'not approved'; registration checks one string before starting the next ceremony; proof checks only nonempty string before notifying the vault owner. Shape, discriminant and semantic consistency checks do not guard these publications.
findings.impact: A malformed or mismatched successful response makes users re-register unnecessarily, shows 'device verified' while the vault remains locked and hides both ceremony actions, or opens an extra authenticator prompt after an unconfirmed registration acknowledgement. An impossible proof string is also announced as successful authentication and delivered to the vault UI although the server rejects that grammar. This is a concrete UI truthfulness/recovery and workflow defect; it does not establish a server access-control bypass.
reproduction: Return HTTP 200 application/json with null, {}, or [] for /api/device?action=status. The shipped module renders '기기 미승인', offers registration and never calls the lock/error path.

Return a status object with schema aleph.device.status.v1, registration not_registered, verified true, canOpenVault true and installIsApproval false. The module renders '기기 확인 완료' and hides registration/authentication actions, with zero onAuthorized calls.

Start explicit registration in the synthetic fixture, then return {registration:'approved'} or a schema/flag/next-step mismatch from registration-verify. The module requests assertion-options and opens the subsequent fake assertion prompt, instead of treating the acknowledgement as unknown.

Return a proof response with the otherwise valid schema/approved/expiry but proof equal to whitespace, 39 base64url characters, 101 base64url characters or 43 plus signs. Actual verifyDeviceGrant rejects each before a DB lookup; initDeviceAccess nevertheless invokes onAuthorized and renders '인증기 확인 완료'.
findings.evidence: The final independent scratch probe executes the unmodified production device module and actual server grant parser with only synthetic DOM, HTTP, identity, authenticator and DB stubs. It reproducibly has 18 failing negative cases and 9 passing controls. The 40/100-character positive controls explicitly preserve the real existing accepted grammar.
proposedFix: Validate each successful device response against its current domain contract before changing state, controls, calling onAuthorized or starting a subsequent authenticator step. Validate required values, types and semantic relationships; do not impose arbitrary restrictions on unrelated extension fields.

For invalid status, use the visible unknown/server-check-failed recovery path, keep the vault locked, hide registration/authentication until a valid status is obtained, and keep manual status refresh usable. Do not interpret unknown payloads as not_registered.

Validate the registration acknowledgement's schema and declared next/proof state before requesting assertion options; retain a failure notice during status rediscovery and preserve existing focus recovery.

Match proof syntax to the existing consumer's 40-100 base64url range rather than hard-coding the currently emitted 43. Preserve existing proof schema/approval/positive expiry checks and existing lifetime/identity guards.

Replace underspecified successful test fixtures with current contract-shaped status/acknowledgement/proof data, add malformed-type/flag/schema matrices and valid boundary controls, then check late-result and keyboard-recovery behavior so validators do not regress the established flow.
findings.analogousPaths: Status, registration acknowledgement and proof result share the cause and are covered here. WebAuthn options are passed through to the existing WebAuthn implementation; no new defect is inferred from a fake authenticator accepting malformed options. Operations and local AI/native views have explicit response validation and did not reproduce this device-specific omission.

findings.title: Partial numeric tokens replace duration/count evidence and invalidate minimum/maximum thresholds
findings.impact: Long elapsed times and invalid negative/fractional counts can become high-confidence blocks and offline deny candidates; valid 10–12 repeated service registrations can be missed. The candidate corroboration layer agrees with the misclassification because the brute-force matcher duplicates the lexical error and sibling builders recompute their decider.
findings.rootCause: Description matching accepts digit suffixes without whole numeric-token boundaries, and some predicates encode thresholds as literal digits instead of parsing a whole quantity and comparing it numerically. Duration regexes truncate to the last 1–3 digits; count regexes truncate to the last 1–5 digits; English account counts match suffixes after signs, decimal points and exponents. Literal [12], 10 and [3-9] tests create the analogous problem in privilege, exfiltration and persistence.

Persistence repeated_unsigned_service_registration specifies minOccurrences 3 and a description of three or more repetitions.
Count fields elsewhere use whole bounded unsigned integer validation; negative/fractional counts are not valid independent evidence and must not be converted to positive suffixes.

C9 semantic checks match the actual status/registration producer and proof consumer. Lifetime acceptance precedes semantic status, registration and proof checks; epoch, status generation and token checks prevent stale responses from producing a new error or successful ceremony. Malformed registration does not advance to assertion. Unknown/malformed status locks and permits explicit refresh. Semantic failure rediscovery preserves its notice while leaving a fresh ceremony to an explicit action. Extension fields are accepted without weakening required fields.

Checked device callbacks against vault locking, session revalidation and proof timer ownership. Pagehide/identity transitions lock and invalidate pending device work; BFCache restore obtains a fresh status. Optional-module lifetime gating prevents late initialization after interruption, and fallback keeps device actions unavailable.

12 integrated scenarios cross malformed registration/proof with identity replacement, pagehide+persisted pageshow, or manual refresh, and an old valid or malformed status body. Recovery response reader is intentionally noncooperative: read remains pending and cancel never settles. A fresh explicit assertion succeeds; resolving the old body afterward causes no additional authorization, lock, request, UI state change or focus movement. No authentication prompt is opened merely by rediscovery. Old reader is cancelled once, lock release is attempted immediately, no second read occurs, and request timers clear.

Re-read final lookup acceptance, map ownership checks, terminal retention and settlement, job deadline propagation, persistence acknowledgment guards, pending-start shutdown and temporary native-capability cleanup. Accepted background work keeps its own controller; later cancel/close/deadline checks gate persistence acknowledgment and final publication. Focused actual manager tests exercise positive and negative final-await timing, retained-flow eviction, deadline/closure, active and starting capacity, monotonic terminal retention and native reclassification.

Compared device semantic handling with AI connection transport and controller ownership. Transport final successful publication retains a lifetime check; controller generation prevents stale status application; confirmed denial distinctions remain intact. Executed final UI-boundary and shared transport tests for late success/failure, cancellation, response and reader disposal, nonsettling cleanup and bounded processing.

Read matching C9 CI logs as separate evidence. Linux log identifies source commit 67dd0620d57698023cbad39d0487be7a904999d6 and records the native pre-header abort, pagehide/restore, module fallback and late-evaluation browser checks. findings.title: Startup readiness does not enforce one monotonic WaitSeconds budget through final acceptance
findings.impact: A backwards wall-clock correction extends the configured startup wait by the correction, while a forward correction can prematurely kill the launcher-owned child. Independently of clock changes, a response obtained after the WaitSeconds budget can still publish startup success. Thus the advertised bounded startup wait is not enforced at the actual success/timeout boundary.
findings.rootCause: The readiness loop derives a relative budget from Get-Date wall time and tests it only before a potentially blocking Invoke-WebRequest. Every probe gets a fresh fixed two-second timeout, failure adds an unconditional 300 ms sleep, and a 200 response sets ready without rechecking elapsed time. These are one root-cause group: no single monotonic operation deadline owns the whole startup-readiness operation.
evidence: Line 134 assigns $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds($WaitSeconds); line 135 compares another Get-Date, rather than elapsed Stopwatch time.
Line 137 permits a two-second probe even with WaitSeconds=1 or less than two seconds remaining.
Line 138 sets $ready=true and breaks on status 200 with no deadline check after Invoke-WebRequest. Lines 145-149 then report success/background completion.

The local runtime-contract test covers supported versions and alternate ports only. Exact C9 Windows CI proves ordinary launcher startup but contains no clock-jump or delayed-readiness boundary experiment.
reproducer: Source-defined late-success case: WaitSeconds=1, a still-running child, first HTTP probe begins before the deadline and returns status 200 at elapsed 1500 ms (within its fixed TimeoutSec=2). The current branch at line 138 accepts success despite elapsed > WaitSeconds. A Windows isolated test can replace Invoke-WebRequest with a synthetic delayed 200 result; no real service is necessary.

Source-defined clock-correction cases: inject Get-Date observations which move backwards by 60 seconds after deadline creation while probes fail, or jump forwards by 60 seconds before the next loop condition. The former extends the loop by roughly 60 seconds; the latter reaches the timeout/kill branch before the elapsed budget is consumed. Mock clock observations; do not change the machine clock.
findings.repair: Use a Stopwatch-based elapsed budget for readiness; recompute remaining time before each probe/delay and recheck the absolute monotonic deadline after probe completion before accepting a 200. Stop and clean up only the launcher-owned child on actual budget expiry. Add isolated PowerShell controls for late 200, exact expiry, backwards/forwards wall-clock changes, and ordinary timely readiness; execute them in the existing Windows CI job without policy override.

findings.title: Inherited Git routing lets the supposedly isolated manifest test modify a different Git directory

locations.role: withHistory supplies cwd but spreads all process.env into mutating Git commands
hash-object -w, mktree and commit-tree write through the inherited repository/object routing
the direct verifier and CLI child also inherit ambient Git routing
related read-only verifier ignores no ambient routing despite an explicit cwd

findings.impact: Running this test from an environment with an absolute GIT_DIR pointing to an existing working repository can reinitialize that directory as bare and add fixture objects there. Its temporary cwd does not provide the promised preservation boundary. The regression may still report success; even where later checks fail, the configuration mutation has already occurred.
findings.rootCause: Git repository/worktree/index/object routing environment variables take precedence over cwd. withHistory copies process.env, then invokes git init --bare and object-writing commands without an isolated Git environment. Its final cleanup removes only the new cwd, leaving externally routed writes behind. The direct helper and CLI verification can operate on the same wrongly selected Git store, allowing the test assertions to pass.

reproduction.scope: Only a disposable synthetic Git directory and test temp directories under review-notes; no actual repository or private file was targeted.
steps: Create a synthetic Git directory with no references or objects; set its core.bare to false to model an existing non-bare configuration.
Run the current node --test test/commit-manifest.test.mjs with GIT_DIR set to that directory and TMPDIR set to a different temporary test-fixture location.
Compare the synthetic Git configuration/object count after execution.

findings.recommendedRepair: Give every temporary-history Git operation an explicit isolated environment that clears inherited repository/worktree/common-dir/index/object routing. Apply the same context consistently to fixture construction, in-process verifyCommitManifest calls and CLI children; sanitizing only git init is insufficient. Avoid temporarily modifying global process.env. Add a negative preservation regression with a separate synthetic existing Git directory and injected routing variables; the fixture tests must still exercise their intended history while leaving external config, refs, index and objects unchanged.
findings.analogousScope: Inventory all Git subprocess sites using cwd as their repository selector, especially the verifier used inside this fixture. Repository-local read-only metadata consumers may need explicit context policy, but this report claims only the reproduced write-capable fixture defect.

findings.title: Aggregating separated observations creates an active candidate during a period supported by neither event
findings.impact: All six offline candidate adapters can return deny for a valid scoped historical context whose timestamp lies after the first observation has expired and before the second observation begins. A later observation retroactively fills an otherwise inactive interval. This is an observed pure-function contract failure, not a claim of live operational enforcement.
findings.rootCause: Each observation first receives the correct15-minute expiry. Grouping then keys only by identity/scope and replaces all temporal evidence with minimum startsAt and maximum expiresAt, without requiring overlapping or touching windows. The resulting single interval is a convex hull rather than the union of valid windows. isActiveDenyCandidate sees only that hull, and evidenceAlertIds retains membership without the corresponding per-event validity intervals.

consumer.role: Checks only the stored half-open aggregate interval; it cannot reconstruct the discarded gaps.

contractBasis.fact: candidateExpiry preserves the exact requested lifetime; all six builders pass15*60*1000 milliseconds for each observation.
The current executable contract requires startsAt equal to the event timestamp, an exact15-minute individual lifetime, deny through the last millisecond, and pass at expiry.

The existing aggregation test merges observations one second apart, which overlap. It builds a batch containing both and queries each original timestamp, including the earlier timestamp; historical queries are supported and are not restricted to times after the latest observation.
Activity is defined by startsAt<=at<expiresAt, so adjacent windows may join without creating a temporal gap.

findings.contractInterpretation: Union semantics is derived from the per-event15-minute half-open validity plus supported historical queries; no current source contract literally says union-of-intervals. The scoped search of XDR implementation, contract tests and current documentation found no stated policy intentionally extending an expired rule retroactively across a gap. Existing tested min/max aggregation covers overlapping observations, where hull and union coincide. This finding does not object to continuous extension when windows overlap or touch, and does not rely on the archived README as a current normative contract.

reproduction.fixtureMethod: Copy a public strong fixture twice, preserve payload/scope, use valid original and -later IDs, and set times10:00 and10:30 UTC. For the first known-CVE fixture only, add a synthetic /notes route because its unchanged original lookup header has no route provenance. No lookup text is altered or executed.
reproduction.expected: pass: neither per-event interval is active, and each individually built candidate actually returns pass.
reproduction.actual: The batch becomes one10:00–10:45 rule and returns deny in all six adapters. Context identity/scope/event IDs are valid and unchanged; they are not malformed or absent inputs.

findings.controls: 72 bounded cases:24 failures are gap-start, gap-middle, gap-last-ms and reversed-input gap queries across six adapters.48 controls pass, including before-first/after-second bounds, both active windows, exact adjacency and overlap. An independent arithmetic oracle checks membership in either [eventAt,eventAt+15min) interval and is cross-checked against the individually built candidate gates.
findings.recommendedFix: Preserve temporal support when aggregating: retain separate disjoint validity windows or per-evidence validity and evaluate the applicable window, merging only genuinely overlapping/touching intervals. Preserve stable scope identity/address equivalence, current evidence-ID requirements, exact half-open endpoints, overlap extension and input-order independence. Do not solve this by banning supported historical queries or broadening the intended lifetime. Update shared/analogous adapter paths and the bounded regression together.
findings.scope: One aggregation root cause in six adapters, represented by24 failures. No additional speculative gap or per-event-ID policy is asserted beyond the reproduced inactive interval.

findings.title: Concurrent startup can report another instance as the newly owned child ready
findings.impact: A second background launch can report success and its own child PID, then exit 0, even though that child never opens the port and subsequently exits with EADDRINUSE. The displayed URL belongs to the first instance. Foreground launch can also announce success before its own child fails. Ordinary overlapping launches are sufficient.
findings.root_cause: The free-port probe releases its listener before initialization and child start, so it reserves nothing. Readiness combines generic HTTP 200 with independently observed child liveness; neither observation ties the answering listener to that process. Actual server module/configuration/engine preparation precedes listen, leaving a valid interval where a child exists but has not bound or failed yet.

location.role: Port preflight binds and immediately releases.
Accepts any HTTP 200 while the owned process remains alive and the deadline is valid.
Starts child after HTTP initialization, publishes success and child PID, and returns 0 in background mode.
CLI preparation and loadEngine precede the final listen call.
Any ordinary Claire instance serves the same generic root asset with status200.

steps: Perform two successful temporary bind-and-release checks for the same ephemeral loopback port before starting either child.
Start the first actual unmodified server CLI and let it bind and serve root200.
Start the second actual unmodified server CLI, representing the second launcher finishing its independent pre-child initialization later.
Immediately request the port while recording that the second owned process is alive both before and after the response.
Observe root200 from the first child, then observe the second child exit1 with EADDRINUSE and no listen-success message; the first child continues serving200.
reproduction.actual_results: 3/3 observations: HTTP200 in 3.251, 2.957 and 3.727 ms; second child alive before/after; second later failed EADDRINUSE/exit1; first remained available.
reproduction.source_inference: Those directly observed values satisfy the existing PowerShell readiness and final liveness predicates. PowerShell success output/exit0 was not executed locally; its possible publication is inferred from the exact unbound acceptance branch.

findings.repair: Require readiness evidence attributable to the retained child and emitted only after that child successfully listens, for example a per-launch correlation value confirmed by a bounded readiness response or a dedicated owned-child readiness channel. Retain absolute deadlines and final liveness checks. An arbitrary delay or another generic200 cannot establish ownership. Keep port-conflict rejection and avoid terminating the competing listener.
findings.validation_needed: Add a deterministic ordinary concurrent-start/port-contention regression, covering a foreign200 while the new child is still alive. Require the second launch to reject without announcing readiness or killing the first, and the uncontended launch to succeed. Verify the repaired production path in matching Windows CI.
findings.ci_implication: The current successful normal single-launch CI fixture does not exercise this contention interval and therefore does not refute the observation.

A separately confirmed UI issue clears the unresolved-cancel marker when a successful status envelope merely reports unknown.

Source comparison: pending-ticket cancellation retains s.ticket after failure, while connected-session cancellation loses s.session; current/operation authority must remain invalidated rather than restoring that session as a fix. findings.title: Connected native cancellation loses its remote target and can falsely confirm a no-op retry
findings.impact: After an already connected native session has an unacknowledged cancellation, an explicit second cancel reports cancelled and the UI states that the server confirmed cancellation, enables a fresh start, and sends no remote request. The first in-flight cancellation also exposes an accepted cancelled/null public DTO to another status caller before acknowledgment. Local access is correctly invalidated; the defect is presenting that local action as confirmed remote cancellation and losing recoverability.
findings.rootCause: cancel captures old=s.session, then invalidate erases s.session and eagerly sets s.state=cancelled. The connected cancellation target survives only in the first invocation local variable. On nonce/cancel failure the state becomes unknown, but no private cancellation-only owner remains. A later cancel sees neither session nor ticket, skips both remote branches and returns cancelled. public status reads the eager state without waiting for the serialized remote exchange.
reproduction: Complete actual producer start/redeem against a synthetic gateway; the browser controller reaches connected.

Hold the first cancellation at nonce, or at cancel after nonce succeeds. producer.status already returns cancelled with null fields and validNativeData accepts it, while no cancellation acknowledgment exists.
Reject the held remote request. Producer/UI become unknown and the UI correctly sets cancelUnconfirmed=true.

Explicitly cancel again. No new nonce or cancel is issued, yet the UI reaches cancelled, renders the cancellation-confirmed message and canStart=true. The synthetic remote session remains active. In the nonce failure path, no remote cancel was ever sent.

evidence.positive_control: A timely acknowledged cancel issues nonce+cancel, ends the synthetic remote session and correctly reaches cancelled.

findings.recommendedRepair: Keep immediate local authorization/operation invalidation. Separate pending remote cancellation ownership from the usable session; retain a private, non-authorizing target for an explicit retry or preserve unknown if confirmation cannot be obtained. Do not publish cancelled during the pending exchange. Only enter confirmed cancelled on supported acknowledgment/authoritative evidence or when there truly was no unresolved remote target. Preserve generation, serialized nonce ownership, deadlines, expiry/close cleanup and no automatic retry. Add the public producer+consumer failure/retry and concurrent-status cases as regressions.
relatedPaths: Pending-ticket cancellation retains s.ticket and must keep its existing behavior.
current, openNativeOperation and receipt operations must never regain authorization from a retained cancellation-only target.
Browser cancel/check/start availability must reflect unresolved cancellation rather than missing local session storage.

findings.title: A native unknown status observation erases unresolved cancellation evidence
findings.impact: After an unconfirmed cancellation the explicit cancellation warning and helpInfo.cancelUnconfirmed=true disappear merely by checking a server state that is still unknown. The generic unknown phase remains, but the UI and diagnostics lose the fact that a requested cancellation has never been confirmed.
findings.rootCause: Native accept unconditionally writes cancelUnconfirmed:false, including server unknown and starting, which it maps to phase unknown. check invokes accept for those shaped successful status envelopes. A transport success is being treated as resolution of the cancellation outcome.
reproduction: Use either failing cancellation scenario in R2-A8-R1-01.
Observe unknown phase with cancelUnconfirmed=true immediately after the failure.
Call the actual controller check; the actual producer status returns unknown.
The phase remains unknown, but state/helpInfo.cancelUnconfirmed becomes false and the cancellation-specific warning disappears, without any remote cancellation acknowledgment.

evidence.source_supported_sibling: The same accept path maps starting to unknown and unconditionally clears the flag; this sibling was source-traced, not separately executed.

findings.recommendedRepair: Preserve pending cancellation evidence across unknown/starting observations and failed or malformed checks. Clear it only on a validated definitive state or the explicitly defined new-flow/reset boundary. Apply a native counterpart of the generic AI controller pending-cancel policy, with public state, message and help-info regressions.

Native failTo preserves the prior flag for failed/malformed checks; keep that behavior.

findings.title: Generic record outcomes become normal-address exemptions and erase independently corroborated candidates
findings.impact: Adding an incomplete row or a well-formed row with no classification/normal-activity evidence removes an existing high-confidence candidate in five offline adapters. findings.rootCause: The four normalSources loops and exfiltration benignDestinations loop treat decide(alert).action === record as positive normal-activity evidence before any equivalent eligibility check. The standalone classifiers also use record for invalid, absent or unrecognized evidence (no_t1190_pattern, no_t1190_signal, no_persistence_signal, no_privilege_signal, no_exfiltration_signal). This overload is then promoted to a batch-wide source/destination veto. Persistence, privilege and exfiltration already distinguish explicit benign reasons from no-signal reasons, but their consumers discard that distinction. Web/known-CVE share generic record reasons and need a genuine normal-evidence predicate rather than a reason-only shortcut.

Current contracts preserve valid following evidence when malformed addresses are present, and deliberately retain shared-address protection for actual normal fixtures. The proposed repair preserves both behaviors and extends the evidence distinction to other invalid/incomplete inputs.

findings.title: Focus recovery regression tests tear down their DOM before their pending create/session flow finishes
findings.impact: The focused recovery/accessibility tests exit unsuccessfully even after their UI assertions pass. This prevents reliable isolated regression checking; source tracing also shows that pending handlers can outlive their own fixture and observe a following fixture’s globals. No production-browser focus failure or server/access defect was established.
findings.root_cause: setup registers an immediate t.after global restoration/deletion at line38. Focus tests start an async create-form handler and await only that session revalidation has begun. Their finally resolves the deferred refresh but does not await the handler’s settlement. Its later finally calls syncCreatePendingState after document has been deleted, producing ReferenceError. Running other tests in the same full file can keep a document installed; that does not make ownership correct.
findings.reproduction: node --test --test-name-pattern='^locking the vault preserves focus moved elsewhere during the lock$' test/session-invalidation-ui.test.mjs
evidence: Initial combined selection: four individual test bodies passed, followed by file-level failure and asynchronous activity after the focus test ended.
Unchanged isolated focus command reproduces exit1: one pass, one file-level fail, ReferenceError: document is not defined.

Observation-only diagnostic confirms syncCreatePendingState ([current-root-inline]:82:22) called from Element.<anonymous> ([current-root-inline]:1719:9), corresponding to shipped HTML lines318 and1955.
Adjacent independent focus test at line529 reproduces the same exception/stack; the two stale-state controls without the focus test pass.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the synthetic fixture explicit ownership of its asynchronous UI handlers/revalidation and wait for bounded settlement or a deterministic completion signal before restoring global DOM/timer state. Apply the same cleanup contract to analogous delayed-refresh cases. Preserve current focus/draft/state assertions and verify these cases individually as well as together. Do not suppress uncaught errors, add arbitrary sleeps, depend on a later test installing globals, or add a product document-existence guard solely to hide fixture teardown leakage.

checks.evidence: Used the previously read, unchanged Attempt 13 protocol and plan; independently verified their hashes and all six procedure helpers before and after this round. Exact main HEAD, fingerprint, clean source/index and empty untracked/unmerged arrays matched. No current Round 2 peer report or verdict was inspected. Existing immutable probes were executed again with new logs; no prior approval or test result substitutes for the executions reported here.

Traced the request Promise.race acceptance check, finally cleanup, whole-cancellation limits and the final outer check. The independent probe advances either wall or monotonic time during the owned request controller abort callback, after successful HTTP processing, consumed body and released reader, but before the outer cancellation continuation. This specifically challenges a final-await boundary that an inner request-only deadline check would miss. Session nonce and ticket acknowledgment paths both reject equality with the absolute deadline.

For both session and ticket targets, a pre-aborted caller withdraws usable local authority and performs zero gateway calls. It leaves unknown public status and a private cancellation-only retry target. Current access is rejected, replacement start is busy, and explicit cancellation retry must actually send the supported target exchange. An expired final acknowledgment is also unconfirmed; remote response arrival alone does not establish timely local success.

Traced serialized current/cancel work, snapshot-based request/operation invalidation, entry generation capture before the clock callback, and closed-state checks. Focused execution blocks an existing current exchange, cancels it, rejects the old operation capability and releases its late response without revival. Closing during cancellation rejects pending work and every subsequent producer operation without more dispatch. A clock callback replacing the flow cannot let the older cancel adopt that generation or send a nonce/cancel for it.

checks.result: Traced the current browser AI/native transports and their server counterparts into the shared response owner. Cancellation reaches the owned controller; late fetch resolution still passes through lifetime.response, so an already closed owner disposes the response. Each outer finally clears its timer and external listener while closing its local lifetime. Fresh tests across these four actual adapters confirmed one discarded late body with no second request. Both throwing and indefinitely pending cleanup preserved the original protocol rejection and allowed public completion.

Checked generation capture, operation ownership and consumer reset together. Producer invalidation snapshots owned requests and operations; operation.close is idempotent, removes its external listener, clears its timer and deletes its registration. Consumer reset advances generation, aborts its own request and stops expiry scheduling while retaining unresolved cancellation state. Five fresh integrated tests exercised settled-operation cancel/close, close during an unfinished cancellation and reset during/after a failed cancellation. Late completion neither reopened a closed producer nor triggered automatic retry; an explicit subsequent retry could resolve the consumer state.

Traced request lifetime through nested engine reads and route publication. Read and overall request budgets remain separately enforced after awaited or synchronous work; successful send checks the overall deadline after metadata construction. Per-read finally removes its listener and timer; request finally removes disconnect listeners, clears request/support timers and aborts lifetime. Server close propagates into connection managers, native host and pending scope reads. Three isolated loopback tests confirmed that synchronous late read results, late request results and metadata-induced deadline crossing cannot publish success.

Cross-checked the root response process-ID marker against the launcher exact single-value comparison and final owned-child/monotonic acceptance. This is startup attribution, not authentication. Saved run45216386995 matches this exact HEAD and completed successfully. Raw logs show Linux root1151/client738 and Windows Git8/client738, all with zero skips. findings.title: Current index describes audit-tagged CI as a limited path although it adds to unconditional baseline checks
findings.impact: A maintainer following the index can expect an audit-tagged push to run only documentation/host checks and reserve full quality checks for ordinary commits/PRs. In fact, it also schedules Linux root regression/build/browser checks and Windows client checks. The index therefore misstates execution scope and contradicts another current guide; no live or security impact is asserted.
findings.rootCause: The index paragraph conflates the limited steps of the optional readonly-audit job with the scope of the complete tagged workflow. The baseline jobs and the current deployment runbook explicitly treat that matrix as additional coverage.
evidence: docs/README.md:96 says audit-tagged changes run only documentation/host observation regression and contrasts ordinary commits/PRs keeping full checks.

Current docs/DEPLOYMENT_DRIFT_RUNBOOK_2026-10-30.md:19 explicitly states the tag never exempts full verification.
findings.recommendation: Keep the workflow unchanged. Rewrite the index paragraph to say baseline quality checks always remain and an eligible audit-tagged push additionally runs the scope-validated three-OS audit matrix. checks.scope: Final result acceptance at deadline equality
checks.evidence: Traced request-level Promise.race acceptance, owned-controller cleanup, the whole cancellation deadline and the outer post-await check. The independent probe advances wall or monotonic time during the successful inner request cleanup callback, after the body is consumed and the reader unlocked. This places expiry after successful inner HTTP work but before outer publication. One millisecond before expiry succeeds; exact equality rejects for both session nonce and ticket acknowledgment paths. A late ticket acknowledgment remains locally unconfirmed, while a late nonce cannot authorize the subsequent cancellation dispatch.

Both target variants send no gateway request for an already-aborted caller and remove usable local session authority. Their public state remains unknown. Current access is unverified, replacement start remains busy, and explicit retry performs the required target exchange. Deadline rejection preserves the same retry behavior. This separates local revocation, request dispatch and remote acknowledgment instead of treating abort as successful remote cancellation.

Held the first cancellation response, then started a replacement whose nonce fails. Both calls reject and state stays unknown. Releasing the earlier successful response still cannot confirm the newer failed generation. A subsequent explicit retry succeeds using the retained target. The source guard binds both generation and cancellation target identity, and only the current generation can publish a failure state.

Invalidation captures the generation and owned request/operation sets before invoking abort callbacks. An abort callback that starts another cancel causes the older cancel to reject with context change while the newer generation performs exactly one cancellation. A callback that closes the producer during replacement start prevents any new start dispatch and leaves status disabled. Late held current responses cannot revive either path.
