No current Round 3 peer report or verdict was accessed. All executions below produced new current-candidate logs; neither prior votes nor earlier probe results substitute for this evidence.

Traced cancellation publication, transport body reading, final acceptance and UI generation/uncertainty guards. The integration uses actual producer, native fetch transport and controller with a synthetic public-envelope bridge. It pauses the browser response halfway through its body after the producer has already confirmed cancellation. Reset or expiry must therefore terminate local ownership without claiming that this screen received a complete valid acknowledgment.

For session and ticket variants, a pending underlying cancel promise does not block UI completion or reader release. Rejected cleanup is handled too. Each acquired body is cancelled once and unlocked; UI uncertainty remains until an explicit status check. That check confirms the producer state without another gateway exchange. No automatic retry or late success publication occurs. Source tracing confirms disposal is idempotent and cleanup settlement is not awaited by request completion.

Traced the generic and native managers from accepted finish into their independent connector work. Both tests observe 202 acceptance, abort the caller signal and verify the job request remains active. Manager close then aborts that request. Releasing its held failure response completes without reopening the job. This checks separation of caller lifetime from accepted job lifetime while retaining manager-owned cancellation.

The native persistence regression first identifies the actual final capability assertion before a timely write, then closes the manager at that same assertion. The positive control writes once; the closed case writes zero times and leaves the manager unavailable. The post-assertion guard closes the reentrancy window. Fresh logs match the counts below; the saved exact CI summary also matches C20 HEAD and completed/success, but remains external evidence.

Deadline expiry is injected through the clock and next body chunk, not measured as a ten-second real-time wait. The pending cleanup gates stay unresolved until after the assertions, directly testing that completion does not await them.

The probe field uiCompletedBeforePendingCleanupSettled is false for the two rejected-cleanup cases because those cases have no pending gate. It is not a failed assertion: both complete, release the reader and pass recovery checks.

checks.observation: Freshly traced all three actual PowerShell spawnSync sites. Each performs one real fixture invocation, retains the non-Windows ENOENT-only skip, and rejects result.error before status and JSON acceptance. Timeout/nonzero execution cannot become an availability skip. Combined diagnostics retain error code/message, status, signal, elapsed time, stderr and stdout. The launcher uses a 30-second interpreter/AST envelope within a documented 75-second fixture guard; it explicitly acknowledges that node:test cannot preempt synchronous spawn.

The expanded fixture envelope does not relax the actual 3000/1000 ms readiness calls. CLI preparation, competing bind failure and registered TERM/KILL teardown remain bounded stages. Production Stopwatch checks include fractional remaining time, final child liveness and strict final attempt/overall deadlines. HTTP uses ResponseHeadersRead and accepts exactly one invariant decimal PID matching the owned process. Initialization precedes child ownership; cleanup disposes responses/requests/clients and coordinates queued cancellation-source disposal without waiting for cancellation callbacks.

Reviewed both manager paths against cumulative resource contracts. Active records and pending starts share the configured maximum of 1–32. Reservations precede asynchronous work and unwind in finally; only terminal history is reclaimed under pressure. Private completion ordering and monotonic retention avoid wall-clock rollback and equal-timestamp ordering problems. Closed managers abort pending work and reject new starts; late continuations must retain current map identity and deadline validity before publication.

Response ownership remains installed before fetch. Late responses are discarded, reader ownership is released immediately and retried after cancellation settlement, and cleanup never awaits an uncooperative cancellation promise. The native reader rejects declared or observed bodies beyond 8192 bytes before copying further chunks, carries shared wall/monotonic deadlines, and clears request timers/listeners and ownership in finally. Source discovery initially used two nonexistent public filenames (rg exit 2); rg --files resolved the actual consumers, with no missing product file implied.

FAIL: 2 tests, 1 passing positive control, 1 failure, 0 skipped. Valid clock rejection cleaned both resources; invalid clock rejection retained one timer and one caller abort listener after producer.close(). Both cases made zero fetch calls. Probe teardown explicitly removed retained synthetic resources.

findings.impact: A rejected operation opening can leave a live timer and caller abort listener that producer.close() cannot reclaim. The timer remains until its configured duration; the external listener remains until that signal aborts. Repeated failures accumulate retained resources. This is demonstrated for the supported injected clock boundary, not claimed for ordinary Date.now().
findings.rootCause: openNativeOperation registers the external listener and timer before p.time(), while constructing/registering op.close() and entering the cleanup try only afterwards. A rejected clock value or thrown clock therefore exits before ownership is enrolled.
findings.reproductionEvidence: a15-r2-reviewer2-open-clock-cleanup.test.mjs calls the actual exported function with a synthetic clock returning NaN and a non-aborted signal. It observes NATIVE_HOST_UNVERIFIED, calls producer.close(), then measures timers=1/listeners=1/fetches=0. The otherwise identical valid-clock control measures 0/0/0. First TAP and exit 1 are preserved in the linked log/results.
findings.repair: Put acquisition under one cleanup owner before any subsequent throwing callback, or validate the clock before acquiring resources while preserving captured-generation and reentrancy checks. Ensure every exceptional exit clears the timer, removes the caller listener and unregisters any partially created operation.

findings.impact: An operation can be acquired but not returned when binding or final host validation fails. Binding failure bypasses login-capability cleanup; final validation failure leaves an unreachable capability in the host operations set until host shutdown.
findings.rootCause: Line 86 calls nativeOperationBinding(loginCap) outside the try that closes loginCap. Line 91 inserts the host capability into operations and s.operations before assertNativeHostOperation, but the catch only closes loginCap and never removes the host registration.
findings.reproductionEvidence: Source-supported analogous paths: nativeOperationBinding invokes operationLifetime, which can reject on expiration, abort or clock failure; assertNativeHostOperation can reject after registration on lifetime, configuration, project or identity validation. No native host process, filesystem configuration or credentials were exercised for this finding.
findings.repair: Move post-acquisition binding validation inside the cleanup region. Retain ownership of any registered host capability until successful return, and close/unregister that capability on final validation failure; otherwise close the acquired login capability. Add narrow failure controls for both boundaries.

Traced native-login.mjs:144–164 against R2-A15-R2-01. The operation and idempotent close owner are registered before clock validation. Listener/timer acquisition, deadline initialization, refresh and final assertion now share the catch that closes the owner. Reentrant invalidation can close the partially initialized operation without adopting a newer generation; original generation validation still occurs before refresh dispatch. Public capability publication remains after final assertion.

Traced native-context.mjs:84–100 and125 against R2-A15-R2-02. Binding validation is inside the acquired-login cleanup region. If a host capability was registered before final validation fails, catch closes that host capability and removes its host-set entry; earlier failures close the login capability directly. closeNativeHostOperation marks closed before cascading cleanup, so repeated closure is idempotent even after host state becomes closed.

Traced manager.mjs:338–379 against the direct C22 acquisition-handoff analogue. The supplier records cap=opened before returning through within/stage, so wrapper rejection cannot lose cleanup ownership. A capability arriving after abort, deadline or shutdown follows the separate close-before-use branch. Failed starts still remove pending controllers and release start reservations in finally; successfully registered flows keep their own capability/controller.

Examined analogous request and lookup boundaries. native-login.mjs:44–61 validates the initial clock before resource acquisition and places later body, parse, clock and final-race acceptance inside response/timer cleanup. manager.mjs:287–306 records current=opened before continuity validation and always closes that temporary capability. http-response.mjs:3–37 disposes late arrivals idempotently and does not await uncooperative stream cancellation.

Rechecked cumulative cancellation and background ownership contracts by source at native-login.mjs:34–43,94–117 and manager.mjs:382–414. Cancellation retains only the private retry target until timely confirmed acknowledgment, rechecks its original generation/deadlines after awaits, and clears targets on close. Accepted background jobs retain their own controller/deadline; manager shutdown and final publication guards remain in place. These adjacent paths were source-reviewed, not counted as additional executed tests.

findings.title: Initial clock evaluation restarts the operation monotonic budget after its timeout timer has already started
findings.impact: An operation can refresh and return a capability after its configured timeout interval has already elapsed, until the pending timer callback eventually runs. C22 fixes exception cleanup, but success acceptance still depends on whether the event loop has dispatched that timer.
findings.rootCause: Line153 starts setTimeout(timeoutMs), then invokes p.time(), and only afterward calculates op.mono=performance.now()+timeoutMs. Elapsed time during that clock callback is omitted from the monotonic guard, so the timer and final assertion use different deadline origins. The wall deadline is also computed from the later clock result.

evidence.observed: With timeoutMs=37, initial clock work advances both clocks by37 ms and no timer callback is dispatched. openNativeOperation returns a capability with one operation timer and one caller listener still owned. The0 ms control also returns a capability, as expected. The probe explicitly closes returned capabilities after recording observations.

findings.repair: Use one immutable monotonic start/deadline captured before invoking the initial supplied clock. Derive timer remaining time and acceptance checks from that same origin, and reject elapsed acquisition before refresh/return. Preserve the newly fixed ownership registration, captured generation and idempotent cleanup.
findings.analogueScope: The adjacent request initial clock precedes its resource acquisition; later clock errors have finally cleanup. The sampler CPU deadline is anchored before its clock read, and the manager outer deadline is captured before capability acquisition. Those guards do not fix this independently callable operation path.

findings.title: Native controller entry overwrites reset during initial deadline construction
findings.impact: The controller can remain in checking with no request running. This busy phase blocks another manual check until another reset, despite the newer reset having restored idle.
findings.rootCause: begin captures a generation and controller, then createNativeDeadline calls the supported clock. If that callback resets the controller, generation advances and the controller is aborted, but begin still publishes its older checking phase. The later call guard avoids dispatch and the final live guard avoids response handling, yet neither undoes the stale entry publication.
findings.reproductionEvidence: The initial case in a17-r1-reviewer2-ui-clock-reset.test.mjs calls ui.reset from the initial clock. Observed phases are idle→checking, resets1, transport calls0, final checking. The normal control makes one call and finishes disconnected.

findings.title: Clock reentrancy bypasses final browser generation acceptance
findings.location: on-client/public/ai-connect.mjs:620–630 check,533–541 accept; analogous native start581–584/redeem598–602/cancel647–648 and generic schedulePoll173–177
findings.impact: A response from the previous generation overwrites reset uncertainty and removes NATIVE_LOGIN_LOCAL_RESET. The same shared acceptance path can republish old approval/connection state or arrange obsolete expiry work after account/page state invalidation.
findings.rootCause: After an await, methods check live(ctx), then call supplied clocks through now(), deadline.left() and accept(). Successful publication is not guarded again after those synchronous callbacks. accept receives g but uses it only later in expiry handling, after state has already been overwritten.
findings.reproductionEvidence: The validation case resets during the now() used to validate a returned status. Observed phases are checking→unknown→disconnected; the final reason becomes null rather than retaining LOCAL_RESET. One synthetic transport call occurred. Generic poll and other native entry points were inspected by source only.
findings.repair: Carry the captured generation through final validation, expiry calculation and timer registration. Recheck it after clock/scheduler callouts and immediately before state publication. Apply the same discipline to schedulePoll and native expiry helpers; a reset must not be overwritten by obsolete work.

findings.title: A reset during initial clock sampling is overwritten by stale starting state
findings.impact: The controller displays a busy starting state after explicit reset although no transport starts. The user receives an inaccurate progress state and cannot rely on that reset to restore usable idle controls.
findings.root_cause: begin captures generation and controller before createNativeDeadline calls supplied clocks, then publishes phase without revalidating ownership. reset increments generation and restores idle during that callback, but stale begin overwrites it. call subsequently rejects the stale generation, leaving no work to complete the displayed state.
findings.reproduction: Inject a valid clock that calls controller.reset() once during start initial deadline creation. Assert zero transport calls and idle. Actual state is starting.
findings.proposed_fix: Sample callbacks into locals; verify captured generation and owned controller after supplied callbacks and immediately before phase publication. Stale setup must return without overwriting reset or a newer operation.

findings.title: Final clock callbacks can publish stale connection or cancellation success after reset
findings.impact: An invalidated request overwrites reset-owned unknown with connected or cancelled. The cancellation case also clears unresolved-cancellation state, contradicting the explicit lifecycle recovery contract.
findings.root_cause: check/cancel validate generation before invoking now and timely. minimalRepair: In disk(), capture const sensorStarted=performance.now() immediately before the existing deadline(operation,...) call, after pendingDisk registration. Pass sensorStarted explicitly to deadline. This replaces its default-argument sample at the same point; it does not add a new origin, reset elapsed time or change the queued statfs ownership.

Use one small disk-local finalizer that invokes checkDeadline(sensorStarted,signal,DISK_READ_TIMEOUT) and returns its already-constructed metric. Route the three post-read result exits through it: wrong-type DISK_INVALID with its stamp, nonpositive/negative capacity DISK_INVALID, and the final converted success-or-invalid result. Construct/stamp/round the metric first, then make the final guard the last supplied-callback boundary before return. This avoids fixing only the successful branch while leaving a sibling final timestamp unchecked.

Keep the finalizer inside the existing try/catch behavior. Existing timeout mapping returns unavailable/value null/DISK_READ_TIMEOUT. checkDeadline checks cancellation first, so abort from the timestamp rejects the overall sample with MEASUREMENT_CANCELLED instead of publishing any metric. Do not introduce a new public helper or alter the shared timer.

Leave pendingDisk assignment, identity-checked clearPending and operation.then(clearPending,clearPending) untouched. A timed-out still-pending read retains its slot; a read that already settled before a finalization timeout has already released that slot. Neither case should trigger an automatic retry or clear another read owner.

Preserve existing error mapping and failed-observation timestamp handling. Once an exception has selected an unavailable result, do not recursively finalize that catch path or let timestamp bookkeeping replace the established sensor failure. The aggregate post-envelope cancellation guard remains the caller-cancellation backstop.

directAnalogueSurvey.result: Already preserves the supplied start through work and final await continuation, disposes its timer/listener and checks positive finite remainders on wakes. The missing check is outside this helper; no extraction/timer change is needed.

CPU captures its sensor start before the first clock, passes it to deadline, then checks after the second CPU read, final timestamp and calculateCpuUsage. That is the direct established pattern. A separate supplied monotonic callback measures sample duration; it must not replace the deadline clock.

Memory has no configured per-read asynchronous budget. Its byte validation and timestamp remain independent; adding a timer/global timeout here would expand the contract and would not repair the disk defect.

All success and invalid-data exits after the read can evaluate metadata/conversion after the helper has retired. A local finalizer closes those siblings with the same start. DISK_READ_IN_PROGRESS occurs before this invocation acquires a read and should remain an immediate unavailable observation without creating a fictitious new sensor budget.

sample() intentionally combines independently timed observations and checks cancellation after final checkedAt. It has no single configured global sensor deadline. Reusing one sensor budget to reject healthy sibling metrics or inventing a new whole-sample timeout would change its partial-result contract.

recommendation.api: Extend only the per-request bounded(work) at370 with an optional discard callback. Forward the same optional argument through sourceCall at521. Supply the matching trusted close function only at the four acquisition call sites.
recommendation.why: This places ownership exactly where Promise.race and final assertAlive can discard a value, covers both already fulfilled and late values, and avoids repeating per-route acquisition logic. Retain existing route finally blocks for values successfully transferred to the caller.
ownershipProtocol: Before dispatch retain the existing initial and queued assertAlive checks. An already aborted request must not call work or discard an unacquired value.

Attach an acquisition observer to the actual work contender before it enters Promise.race. On fulfillment record the value with an explicit owned flag, including falsy values; do not wait until the outer await assigns its result.
If the wrapper has already retired, the observer disposes that late value immediately. Otherwise the wrapper owns it while the race and final assertAlive are pending.

Only after final assertAlive succeeds mark the value transferred and clear local ownership immediately before returning. Normal route assignment then receives the original object unchanged, and its existing finally performs exactly one close.

On every failed exit mark the owner retired before invoking discard, take/clear the captured value before its close callback, and detach the abort listener. An abort interleaving, repeated callback or late continuation cannot invoke close twice. Keep the work contender observed even after the race loses so late rejection cannot become an unhandled promise.

Cleanup must not call new clocks, assertAlive, retry work or translate the recorded failure. Use the existing canonical timeout/cancel cause. The production close functions are synchronous and idempotent, but ownership should still guarantee once-only invocation rather than rely on that idempotence. If cleanup exceptions are contained, preserve the original failure; do not replace it with provisioning pending.
recommendation.sourceCallBoundary: Current sourceCall does not add a success-side guard after bounded returns; it only returns the value or adapts a rejection. Forwarding discard therefore covers its acquisition gap. Keep its existing request-error policy and do not add new cleanup-time checks that could alter the decisive cause.
recommendation.learnerSupportBoundary: The current acquisition sits before the route try/finally. With the proposed owner, rejection means no value was transferred; successful return is followed only by assignment and entry into the existing try, so optional discard covers the demonstrated gap without moving the block. Moving acquisition into the try may clarify scope but is not required for this minimal fix; moving try alone does not close late-return values.
recommendation.alternative: A small explicit acquisition owner wrapping each supplier can also work, but must capture before outer guards and close late arrivals. Four duplicated setters/flags plus moving the learner try are larger and easier to diverge than one optional ownership facility.

crossRuntimeLauncherRepair.rootCause: The fixture registered on the token supplied by HttpClient to its handler, which is a linked transport token rather than the original source owned by ReadinessProbe. Framework SetTaskCompleted publishes tcs.TrySetResult before disposing the linked source; an inline await continuation can dispose the HttpClient while that link is still live. HttpClient disposal cancels its internal pending-request source, so the handler callback may run after a successful response without cancelling the original source. Modern HttpClient finishes linked-source cleanup in its async finally before completing the task. The old assertion treated the internal cleanup signal as an explicit caller cancellation.
crossRuntimeLauncherRepair.repair: Record the original source IsCancellationRequested exactly, independently of transportCancellationObserved. Assert both sources initially uncancelled, the five asynchronous test paths still pending before their explicit action, original-source false for timely/unready/send-failure and true for late/cancelled/blocked-cancel. Keep transport delivery positive for all three explicit cancellation paths; normal post-completion transport observation is a boolean whose value may differ by runtime.

designAdvice.scope: Start with create-form submit ownership in this one fixture: all eight confirmed neighboring paths start that same handler. No other handler leak was independently reproduced in this survey.
designAdvice.completion: Wait for actual handler settlement after the tests release their deferred response. aria-disabled, sessionCalls and arbitrary extra ticks do not prove handler completion; session identity changes can reset state before finally.
designAdvice.semantics: If wrapping registration, preserve callback this, callback identity/capture matching, duplicate and once behavior, remove behavior, synchronous return/throw and native dispatchEvent boolean return. designAdvice.meaningfulRegressions: After the owner freezes the repair, execute the original eight affected cases in focused child runs (and together) against the new fixture. In a separately owned copy, substitute only the original fixture and retain the original test selection: expected failure must be the post-test DOM ReferenceError, not an import/path error. checks: Read repository AGENTS and the current production native-login implementation. Verified the two assigned frozen hashes before/after. Source, index and prior evidence remained unchanged; other owners continue separate mutable work.

Read the original independent eight-case probe and the first owner replay against budgetSample. That replay preserves seven passes and one failure: the local-wall TIMEOUT case now passes, but receipt expiry returns EXPIRED while the subsequent proof assertion still succeeds.

Traced all three direct native timeout paths: serializedCurrent line 46 directly fails the waiter; request line 73 directly aborts its controller; openNativeOperation line 187 directly aborts with its private expiry reason. All use potentially fractional remaining time without checking the relevant absolute deadline when the callback fires.

Checked official Node timer documentation: fractional delays are truncated to an integer, and exact callback timing is not guaranteed. A timer callback is therefore a wake-up opportunity, not proof that a higher-resolution absolute ceiling has been reached.

Created a two-case direct-native probe that retains the immutable synthetic fixture and invokes actual production request callbacks under a small scheduler implementing documented integer truncation. No UI code was imported or executed.

tests.kind: Owner first replay, independently read; not my new execution
tests.failure: Original proof timer test line 65: Missing expected exception after the request already rejected EXPIRED. The original local-wall classification test now passes.

tests.earlyCase: With proof deadline 60 ms and request start 0.25 ms, production requests 59.75 ms. Truncation schedules 59 ms; callback at monotonic 59.25 rejects EXPIRED, aborts the request, and suppresses receipt-issue, while assertNativeOperation still succeeds. The explicit pending-before-deadline assertion fails.
tests.equalityControl: The same production callback delivered at monotonic 60 rejects EXPIRED, proof validation rejects EXPIRED, and the longer operation remains valid. This control passes.

findings.impact: A still-valid request/proof can be rejected as expired before either absolute ceiling is reached. The directly executed consequence is premature receipt cancellation and inconsistent proof validity. Early queue retirement and operation abort are source-derived analogues, not separately executed claims.
findings.rootCause: The implementation equates timer delivery with expiry. Remaining monotonic durations are fractional, while Node truncates timer delays. The callback unconditionally fails or aborts instead of rechecking the absolute clock/monotonic ceilings. The budgetSample classification repair does not address this separate pre-existing timer assumption.
findings.oracleAssessment: The original assertion expresses a valid contract: a proof-expiry result should agree with the actual proof ceiling. Its observed failure cannot be dismissed by relabeling the probe flaky or retrying. The original log did not record the exact fractional remaining duration; the deterministic counterexample establishes a supported mechanism consistent with that observation without claiming to recover its precise timing.
findings.repair: Use a small owned timeout mechanism across all three paths. Schedule a positive remainder with an integer ceiling, recheck the relevant absolute deadline when awakened, and rearm only if time remains. Keep at most one owned timer; detach the fired token before replacement; prevent a disposed or retired owner from rearming. Preserve single-sample outer-before-local classification, private expiryReason identity, external CANCELLED, request-local TIMEOUT, queue ordering and exactly-once settlement.
findings.ceilTradeoff: Ceiling removes the documented fractional-truncation cause but is not itself an absolute-deadline check. Rechecking and rearming makes the contract explicit under timer granularity and scheduling variation; no generic async framework or arbitrary retry loop is needed.

results: Positive control passed: proof deadline remains 60ms with wall fixed at 100000. At exactly 60ms the request and proof reject EXPIRED while the longer operation remains valid until explicit close.

findings.impact: Producer shutdown can be reported to a pending caller as expiration of a still-fresh proof/operation. This is an observable error-cause inconsistency; no resource leak, successful late publication or additional request was observed.
findings.rootCause: During timer remaining()->alive()->budgetSample()->clock(), producer.close() changes closed/generation state and invalidate() aborts captured request controllers before captured operations. The request abort listener runs synchronously while its operation signal is not yet aborted and timerFailed is still false. abortFailure() does not inspect current producer/generation ownership and commits the historical timeoutCode (EXPIRED). Later operation cancellation and the active() DISABLED error cannot replace the already rejected aborted promise.
findings.contractBasis: The implementation separates actual outer expiry, local TIMEOUT and lifecycle invalidation. Neither expiry ceiling is reached in this reproduction. The oracle deliberately accepts CANCELLED, CONTEXT_CHANGED, DISABLED or UNVERIFIED rather than demanding one exact shutdown spelling; it rejects the false assertion of TIMEOUT/EXPIRED. Existing source active() independently recognizes closed state as DISABLED.

reproduction.expected: A lifecycle invalidation error; no expiry assertion before either deadline.
reproduction.actual: NATIVE_HOST_EXPIRED; zero active timers, zero new timers during close, only receipt-nonce dispatched.

designPrinciples: Treat supported clock, monotonic, scheduler, clear-scheduler, onChange/onInvalidate and abort listeners as synchronous callouts that can replace the current generation. Preserve a captured owner across every such boundary.
Detach the exact old controller/timer from shared state before invoking abort/clear callbacks. Cleanup must not null or cancel a replacement controller/timer installed during those callbacks.

Native begin must retain its captured generation across old cleanup, new controller assignment and deadline construction; a stale begin cannot publish a busy phase or start transport. Later callers must not clear newer monoExpiry/state after a failed stale begin.

Native call must recheck generation/signal after deadline.left before dispatch. Final response validation and expiry calculation must recheck before state publication. accept must enforce its g argument itself; subsequent scheduleExpiry must not install obsolete timers after onChange reentrancy.

Native expiry and generic polling should validate generation before and after clock/scheduler callouts; returned timer ownership must be retained or immediately released if acquisition is invalidated. markExpired and lost notifications must not mutate a newer flow.

Survey both native and generic controllers together: generic schedulePoll has a source-supported analogous clock/reset gap; generic request entry after onChange and abort ownership transfer need bounded original-source probes before repair. Avoid changes to external result shapes or cancellation-confirmation semantics.

Sampler final checkedAt must be evaluated before the final signal check. Survey earlier clock/sensor callbacks to ensure cancellation cannot turn into an unavailable/successful completed envelope; preserve truthful partial data and original numerical/time contracts.
regressionPlan: Preserve all existing first probes/reports; execute the same positive/negative UI and sampler probes unchanged after repair.
Use meaningful bounded matrices across native start/redeem/check/cancel and generic start/finish/refresh/cancel, targeting clock/reset, explicit replacement and controller/timer ownership handoffs.

Include onChange/abort/clearTimer/setTimer reentrancy only where the source-supported ownership path establishes a concrete risk; positive controls must preserve normal status/current, manual retry and uncertain cancellation behavior.
Inspect actual resources before fallback reset/close so cleanup cannot hide errors. Keep each owned timer/controller identity observable; no exact-delay-only timer filters.
Freeze all source once implementation complete; independent verification, full local suites, exact candidate CI and a fresh three-round formal attempt follow. No prior vote counts.

callbackBoundaryInventory.callback: clock / monotonic: native entry and request acceptance
callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: Deadline construction/left(), now() and returned-data validation run after a generation capture or last live check. Reset/replacement can therefore invalidate entry, dispatch or acceptance synchronously.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Keep the original action deadline; check ownership after each supplied-clock computation and immediately before transport/publication. call must recheck after deadline.left(), even when it returns positive.

callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: expired(), accept expiry calculation and scheduleExpiry can resume after reset. accept currently receives g without enforcing it before publication.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Snapshot relevant state/expiry into locals; calculate without shared writes; enforce g inside accept and after each clock boundary. Guard redeem eligibility after expired(). Preserve the monotonic origin before wall-clock work.

callbackBoundaryInventory.callback: clock: generic polling; both helpInfo methods
callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: Generic poll clock can overwrite reset with timeout or register obsolete work. helpInfo only constructs a return value and is not a state/task publication path.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Guard schedulePoll before and after clock. Inventory helpInfo but do not expand a state-machine repair into an unproven diagnostics redesign.

callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: The state is committed before the synchronous callback, which may reset/start/cancel another generation. Subsequent request, timer or lost-notification work must not continue for the old generation.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Use a private generation-aware publication helper with a post-callback current-generation result. Callers must honor it; do not roll back the newer callback-created state. Preserve callback exception propagation while cleaning only captured resources.

callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: Notification can synchronously replace/reset the flow before begin or following publication.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Capture the intended generation before notification and stop if it changes. Notify lost only while the just-accepted/expired transition is still owned. Preserve existing synchronous notification and caught callback-error behavior.

callbackBoundaryInventory.callback: setTimer / clearTimer: generic poll and native expiry
callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: Clear can reenter before shared field is nulled; a factory can reset before its returned handle is stored; an old callback currently nulls a newer timer handle.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Use exact timer-owner records, detach before clear, register the record before invoking the factory, and retire/clear only that record after return. Callback must check record identity and generation before touching the shared slot.

callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: abort() synchronously invokes listeners; clearing controller afterward can erase a nested operation. A transport may also synchronously reenter before its promise settles.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Detach captured controllers before abort. Capture request identity/body before callouts; carry g into generic call; recheck before dispatch and after await. Dispose only the old owner even if callbacks install a new one.

callbackBoundaryInventory.risk: end detaches its own controller correctly, but abort listeners can change state after a return-state expression has already been evaluated in the surrounding try. This is a source-derived analogous candidate, not an additional established finding.
callbackBoundaryInventory.rule: Include one bounded original-source control if needed to determine whether the public returned state becomes stale; keep final cleanup and any final returned-state snapshot ordered consistently without changing method signatures.

repairSequence.change: Introduce small private ownership primitives, not a new framework. Capture/detach all old controller/timer resources before the first abort/clear callout in a reset or new-operation cleanup. Finish disposal of those captured resources even if generation changes, but never read/clear a replacement owner afterward.

Give generic call a captured generation/context. Check it after abort cleanup and before transport. Snapshot connectionId and terminal phase before callbacks so an old finish/cancel cannot borrow a new flow. Add checks after starting/finishing/cancelling onChange and after stopPoll; preserve the existing normal-completion signal behavior.

Make native begin own its context before deadline/onChange callouts and return a clearly stale/null outcome when invalidated. Every caller must stop immediately on that outcome. Put monoExpiry resets inside the owned entry transition; remove unguarded start/cancel assignments after begin. If a clock/onChange throws, close the captured owner before preserving the existing error propagation.

Native call: current check, deadline.left(), current check, then dispatch. At final acceptance, validate DTO/time into locals, recheck generation, and let accept enforce g internally before clocks and before committing monoExpiry/state. Retain final deadline acceptance after expiry calculations rather than accepting work that consumes the remaining budget.

Make failTo, markExpired, applyStatus and both scheduling paths generation-aware after cleanup and onChange. A stale failure must not erase a replacement state. Check generation after native expiry eligibility and invalidation callbacks. Preserve local reset uncertainty and cancellation warnings.

Represent each scheduled timer with a private token containing generation, handle-ready, retired/fired and cleared flags. recommendations.topic: Separate caller waiting from the actual serialization tail
recommendations.detail: Checking the ceiling only when currentTail.then(work) starts suppresses late dispatch but cannot settle a queued caller while a preceding request remains pending. Keep currentTail tied to the original queued work. A separate caller waiter may reject on its own remaining-budget timer or external abort, clear its listeners/timer, and mark its private entry retired. Check that flag before executing the queued work, so it stays inert even if a synthetic clock later moves backward or another operation timer is withheld. Never advance currentTail from the early caller race, which would overlap nonce-dependent work.

recommendations.topic: Classify direct checks and asynchronous timer/abort paths consistently
recommendations.detail: Current request abort rejection bypasses alive() and chooses CANCELLED/TIMEOUT. Updating only initial/alive comparisons therefore misses real timer delivery. Preserve explicit caller cancellation as CANCELLED, a shorter request-local timeout as TIMEOUT, operation/proof exhaustion as EXPIRED, and cancel-exchange exhaustion as TIMEOUT. Carry the stop cause privately; do not trust arbitrary external signal.reason or globally relabel all aborts EXPIRED. Ensure classification cannot throw out of an abort event handler: settle the owned promise once and always detach resources.

recommendations.topic: Use distinct lifetime and proof ceilings without changing refresh permission
recommendations.detail: For refresh, carry the operation mono ceiling and wall min(operation deadline, captured session expiry when available). Do not include the old proof deadline/session.mono, because refresh intentionally renews expired proof. For receipt, additionally bound wall by captured session proof/expiry and mono by captured session.mono; a receipt already requires fresh proof before and after work. Capture those values immutably rather than consulting a subsequently replaced session. Direct current() without a native operation need not acquire a new public timeout contract merely for this repair.

recommendations.topic: Preserve callback ordering and validate the last clock-consuming step
recommendations.detail: Do not insert a wall-clock callback immediately before captureSession: the existing proof regression deliberately arms its next callback from response cleanup. Reuse an already sampled time or let captureSession validate the carried limit using its own sample. After the last clock-consuming validation, recheck generation/signal and receipt session identity before publishing. If a new clock callback is added after captureSession, also check the newly captured proof/expiry, since that callback can expire fresh evidence even when the broader operation budget remains. Avoid extra sampling when the existing sample suffices.

recommendations.topic: Retain ownership and error semantics through all direct consumers
recommendations.detail: Thread the ceiling through openNativeOperation and refreshNativeOperation, both serialized refresh requests, and issueNativeReceiptTicket through nonce/issue and final acceptance. The formal counterexample observed EXPIRED but asserted only error existence plus the dispatch list; new focused regressions should deliberately lock the chosen classification.

checks.result: The shared timer consumes and clears its actual token before evaluating the remaining budget, rounds a positive fractional remainder upward, and rearms only while still owned. A new independent probe combines initial callback cost, a submillisecond remainder, repeated early delivery, a stale callback and equality expiration. It checks every actual token is cleared exactly once and no token remains active before fallback teardown.

checks.subject: First terminal cause under synchronous cancellation reentrancy

contract: Keep arm(initialRemaining) so extracting the helper does not add an initial injected-clock read or reorder established acquisition checks.

Caller remaining() must check current ownership/cancellation and return a positive finite exact remainder or throw its exact terminal cause. A non-positive budget must be mapped to the domain cause, not silently rearmed. Preserve falsy thrown values via explicit failure state.

Ceil positive scheduling delays; on wake validate the captured token, detach and clear it before resampling, then rearm at most one token only if still owned. Completion, cancellation, close and replacement all dispose idempotently.

Never recreate an absolute deadline from now during rearm. The helper owns scheduling only; it does not choose TIMEOUT versus EXPIRED versus CANCELLED, abort unrelated work or release a real serialization tail.
sharedUtilityRecommendation.alternatives: Private helpers avoid one new served asset but duplicate the already problematic invariant across four domains. Extending http-response.mjs would avoid a new route but mix generic sensor/manager timers into an HTTP-named response module; a dedicated small utility gives clearer ownership. Fixed relative timers need not be migrated merely for uniformity.

conclusion.established: The browser harness readiness predicate can accept a legitimate queued operations refresh while assertRecovery immediately requires the refresh control to be enabled. This synchronization defect is deterministically reproduced with the unchanged operations controller and unchanged request trace, and independently with the full root inline authentication flow.
conclusion.productFinding: No persistent product failure is established by these probes. The queued request completes, the control becomes enabled, and the device fallback remains visible with disabled device actions and a locked vault.
conclusion.actualC13Limit: C13 records only operationsUsable=false, not visibility, native disabled, aria-disabled, status, trace state or the active scenario. The delayed anonymous-session completion is a source-supported and reproduced explanation, not a uniquely observed reconstruction of that CI execution.

actualEvidence.observation: AssertionError at assertRecovery line352, invoked by the first beforeRelease snapshot at main line370. Expected operationsUsable=true; actual false.
actualEvidence.inference: The step fails before the deadline scenario's required real 10000ms wait could complete. Together with the scenario order, this identifies evaluation-failure as the strongly supported failing scenario; the script did not print its mode.

actualEvidence.observation: C12's operations browser step printed all three PASS lines: chart, strict request lifecycle and two module recovery scenarios. This does not imply the overall C12 workflow passed.

sourceFlow.fact: The harness first observes successful operations text and native trace.active===0; in another Runtime.evaluate it observes the device failure text; in a third call it reads the recovery snapshot.
operationsUsable additionally requires the control to be rendered, not natively disabled and not aria-disabled=true. These conditions were not part of the earlier readiness predicate.
Independent bootstrap awaits restoreSession. A 401 response makes restoreSession call invalidateSession at1129-1131.
invalidateSession invokes renderAuth. renderAuth finishes by dispatching aleph:session, even for the anonymous-session invalidation path.

The session listener calls scheduleRefresh. It sets aria-disabled=true immediately and queues a zero-delay task. Until that task runs, the previous successful status text and native trace.active===0 can both remain true.
The scheduled refresh changes the status to observing, reads and validates the response, renders success, then re-enables the control in finally if it still owns the current generation.
trace.active decreases at native fetch settlement (headers or rejection). It intentionally does not represent a queued refresh, response body completion or final UI readiness.
The device fallback only reveals its panel, changes device guidance and disables the three device actions. It does not disable the operations button.
The aria-disabled refresh control uses opacity .65 and a wait cursor. This busy style does not itself make the control invisible.

The connected session or pending ticket moves to a single frozen private cancellation target. invalidate removes usable session authority and closes owned operations. Pending/failed cancellation publishes unknown with null public fields, start/redeem are blocked while unresolved, current/openNativeOperation cannot reuse the target, and explicit retry performs a new remote nonce/cancel or ticket cancel. Only supported HTTP200 acknowledgment or a genuinely empty producer confirms cancellation; HTTP202 remains unknown. The new target is cleared on acknowledgment or close, not treated as authority or canceled merely by local expiry.

Native accept retains unresolved cancellation for server unknown and starting, which project to unknown. Failed/malformed observations preserve the marker. Cancel marks uncertainty at entry; reset during or after a failed cancel keeps that uncertainty. Confirmed states clear it. State, nativeLoginView warning and helpInfo remain consistent.

Traced a single wall/monotonic cancel budget across queued work, nonce, cancel and outer acceptance. Request inherits the remaining budget; entry clock reentrancy is checked before target capture. Invalidation snapshots old requests/operations and returns its own generation, preventing an older reentrant caller from adopting replacement work. Closure and generation checks remain after time callbacks and awaits.

Nine scenarios inject monotonic expiry, close or a replacement cancel during the owned request final abort cleanup, after the request own final success check and before the producer serialized await returns. Covered session nonce, session cancel and ticket cancel. Every stale outer operation rejects with TIMEOUT, DISABLED or CONTEXT_CHANGED; expired operations retain an explicit retry target, closed producers dispatch no new work, replacement cancels own the final result, and all request timers clear.

c11TestRepair.rootCause: The fixture registered on the token supplied by HttpClient to its handler, which is a linked transport token rather than the original source owned by ReadinessProbe. Framework SetTaskCompleted publishes tcs.TrySetResult before disposing the linked source; an inline await continuation can dispose the HttpClient while that link is still live. HttpClient disposal cancels its internal pending-request source, so the handler callback may run after a successful response without cancelling the original source. Modern HttpClient finishes linked-source cleanup in its async finally before completing the task. The old assertion treated the internal cleanup signal as an explicit caller cancellation.

root_cause.reference_source_observation: Framework HttpClient links the caller token to its pending-request source. SetTaskCompleted publishes the response before disposing the linked source; HttpClient.Dispose cancels the pending-request source. A completion continuation can therefore observe transport cancellation during normal client cleanup without cancelling the original caller source.

findings.rootCause: The workflow source assertion matches /  test-and-build:\n/ against unnormalized text. A valid CRLF line contains a carriage return before newline, so the linux block is undefined and assert.ok(linux) fails. The YAML behavior and intended Git fixture context are unchanged.

formalRoundResolutions.cause: The free-port probe releases its listener before initialization and child start, so it reserves nothing. Readiness combines generic HTTP 200 with independently observed child liveness; neither observation ties the answering listener to that process. Actual server module/configuration/engine preparation precedes listen, leaving a valid interval where a child exists but has not bound or failed yet.
formalRoundResolutions.requiredFix: Require readiness evidence attributable to the retained child and emitted only after that child successfully listens, for example a per-launch correlation value confirmed by a bounded readiness response or a dedicated owned-child readiness channel. Retain absolute deadlines and final liveness checks. An arbitrary delay or another generic200 cannot establish ownership. Keep port-conflict rejection and avoid terminating the competing listener.

steps: Perform two successful temporary bind-and-release checks for the same ephemeral loopback port before starting either child.
Start the first actual unmodified server CLI and let it bind and serve root200.
Start the second actual unmodified server CLI, representing the second launcher finishing its independent pre-child initialization later.
Immediately request the port while recording that the second owned process is alive both before and after the response.
Observe root200 from the first child, then observe the second child exit1 with EADDRINUSE and no listen-success message; the first child continues serving200.

report.rootCause: Four normalSources loops and one benignDestinations loop treated every locally computed record action as affirmative normal evidence. Three classifiers already distinguish positive normal reasons; their early benign branches nevertheless do not establish complete observation provenance. changes.purpose: One exact module-to-positive-reason allowlist plus common observation provenance. Callers cannot configure a generic no_* reason as acceptable.

Add private, bounded affirmative-normal predicates at the existing final record path after all block/alert checks. Add normal_web_activity and normal_application_activity only for supported completed normal-operation descriptions and complete raw request evidence without existing suspicious signals. Reuse the existing normalized/decoded URL or HTTP header/query fields; no second HTTP parser, extra export, output field, import or numeric-grammar change.

Require the shared normal-evidence guard and the existing module provenance validators before adding an address to an exemption set. Web/known-CVE require an existing safeRoute; persistence/privilege require the existing normalized agent and reader-valid account; exfiltration requires its existing valid agent/account/destination plus common source/time evidence. Caller proposals remain irrelevant to this locally recomputed normal decision.

Add primitive-string guards before the preexisting candidate-loop ID regexes. A malformed or coercible ID rejected by the normal guard must also be skipped without conversion or Symbol exceptions when the candidate loop reaches it. Existing ID patterns are unchanged.

39 public API regression groups covering all 44 original normal fixtures, sparse/no-signal/weak input, required metadata/type/coercion, exact existing canonical address semantics, description completeness/redaction, independent proposal handling, normal narrative versus actual raw HTTP signals, and unread/oversized/ill-typed HTTP material.

report.root_cause: The fixture restored global DOM state before its create-form submit handler finished processing the deferred refresh. Existing tests asserted the intermediate focus state, then resolved refresh in finally without owning the actual event handler completion. The handler later reached syncCreatePendingState against removed globals. Neighboring test fixtures could mask this lifetime error.
changes: Track only actual Promise results from create-form submit listeners in this fixture. Native dispatchEvent is unchanged; wrappers return the original callback value and preserve function this and object.handleEvent invocation. Stable callback wrappers let native EventTarget retain capture/once/duplicate-registration/removal behavior.

Wait in t.after for all currently started submit completions using allSettled, repeating if a handler started another owned submission. A single 5-second timer imported from node:timers remains real despite mocked globals. An unresolved handler fails cleanup rather than waiting without limit.

Record callback rejection and throw AggregateError after all owned submissions settle, while continuing to return the original Promise to EventTarget so its existing rejection behavior is retained. Restore globals in finally even if cleanup fails.

Add one child-process regression selecting the original failing focus test alone. Copy the environment and exclude NODE_TEST_CONTEXT case-insensitively; preserve the parent environment. The exact name filter excludes the new parent regression, preventing recursion, and assertions require one actual pass with zero skips.

All eight existing delayed-refresh family tests and their UI assertions remain unchanged. No product document guard, arbitrary tick delay, sleep, button-state completion heuristic or broad EventTarget replacement.

designAdvice.scope: Start with create-form submit ownership in this one fixture: all eight confirmed neighboring paths start that same handler. No other handler leak was independently reproduced in this survey.
designAdvice.completion: Wait for actual handler settlement after the tests release their deferred response. aria-disabled, sessionCalls and arbitrary extra ticks do not prove handler completion; session identity changes can reset state before finally.
designAdvice.semantics: If wrapping registration, preserve callback this, callback identity/capture matching, duplicate and once behavior, remove behavior, synchronous return/throw and native dispatchEvent boolean return. Do not suppress rejected work; a drain failure must make the test fail and restoration must still run in finally. Keep timeout bounded using a real captured timer because this fixture stubs global timers.
designAdvice.scopeLimit: The submit handler launches void loadNotes on some paths. Owning the submit Promise does not claim ownership of that detached work. Do not describe this fix as tracking all page tasks.
designAdvice.meaningfulRegressions: After the owner freezes the repair, execute the original eight affected cases in focused child runs (and together) against the new fixture. In a separately owned copy, substitute only the original fixture and retain the original test selection: expected failure must be the post-test DOM ReferenceError, not an import/path error. A small child-process regression guard can make independent case lifetime observable even when the whole suite would mask it; this is a proposal here, not an executed validation.

finding.impact: A capability acquired by native start could escape the manager’s failure cleanup when cancellation or deadline acceptance occurred after the supplier returned it but before the outer assignment completed. The public request correctly returned 504 and made no later read/fetch, yet the acquired capability received no close call. Actual OS resource retention was not exercised; the missed lifecycle release is directly demonstrated using the existing synthetic native dependency.
finding.rootCause: cap = await stage(...) assigned ownership only after two surrounding promise boundaries. within can replace the fulfilled acquired value with ABORTED/TIMEOUT, and stage can reject its final liveness check. In either case the enclosing catch sees cap as undefined. The supplier’s earlier late-open guard covers an already late acquisition, but not cancellation arriving after that guard and before the outer assignment.
finding.reproduction: The standalone probe preserves the existing native() and timing() fixture mechanics and loads actual current manager source, replacing only the Windows native-context dependency. From a successful open it queues a second-microtask abort or sets monotonic time to the exact 10 ms start deadline. Both original-source cases returned 504 with fetches=reads=0 and an aborted request signal, but close count was 0 instead of 1. A timely positive control passed.

changes.description: Record cap = opened inside the successful supplier before it returns to within/stage; the outer call only awaits stage. Preserve the immediate late-open close/throw branch, all deadline/result classifications, original capability-opening budget and existing catch/finally cleanup. This gives the outer failure owner a stable reference even when the promise result is discarded.

Add one regression group with timely, abort and exact-deadline cases.
